title: Section 898(c) Transition Rule for Allocating Foreign Taxes and Section 960(d)(4) Foreign Tax Credit Disallowance
summary: The IRS and Treasury propose rules on allocating foreign taxes for certain foreign corporations affected by repeal of the one-month deferral election, and on disallowing foreign tax credits on certain distributions of previously taxed earnings and profits. Affected taxpayers may comment by 2026-09-17. The proposal applies to taxpayers operating through certain foreign corporations and those claiming the foreign tax credit.

title: Loans to Executive Officers, Directors, and Principal Shareholders of Member Banks; Bank Holding Companies
summary: The Federal Reserve issued a proposal to modernize Regulation O for member banks and bank holding companies. It would update and index dollar thresholds, codify existing interpretations, clarify insider lending and related control tests, and streamline reporting and disclosure requirements. Comments are due by 2026-10-05.

title: Regulatory Modernization and Relief for Mutual Holding Companies
summary: The Federal Reserve has issued a notice of proposed rulemaking to modernize Regulation MM for mutual holding companies and amend the capital rule for certain mutual capital instruments. It would reduce or remove several requirements on MHC formations, conversions, post-conversion restrictions and charter structures, and codify model term sheets. Comments are due by 2026-10-05.

title: OCC Rules Regarding the Availability of OCC Information
summary: The OCC has proposed changes to its information-disclosure rules for national banks, Federal savings associations, Federal branches and agencies of foreign banks, and other OCC-supervised entities. The proposal would clarify when non-public OCC information and confidential supervisory information may be disclosed, update FOIA request procedures, and add an expedited FOIA process. Comments are due by 2026-10-05.

title: Extensions of Credit to Insiders
summary: The FDIC has proposed to raise the quantitative limits for certain extensions of credit to insiders at FDIC-supervised institutions, including higher thresholds for executive officers and for insider loans needing board approval, and to add periodic indexing. Comments are due by 2026-10-05. It applies to state nonmember insured banks, foreign banks with insured branches, and state savings associations.

title: Conflicts and Affiliations
summary: The CFTC is proposing new and amended rules for FCMs, SEFs, DCMs and DCOs on affiliate conflicts, disclosure, financial oversight and safeguards for impartiality, including limits on resource and information sharing. Market participants in scope can comment by 2026-10-05. No obligations apply yet because this is a proposal.

title: Employer Contributions to Trump Accounts and Nondiscrimination Rules for Dependent Care Assistance Programs
summary: Treasury/IRS has issued a proposed rulemaking on employer contributions to Trump accounts and nondiscrimination rules for dependent care assistance programs. Employers offering these programs and employees participating in them are in scope. Comments and requests to speak are due by 2026-09-25, and the public hearing is set for 2026-10-15.

title: CMA proposes removing 27 market remedies in part or full following review
summary: The CMA is consulting on a provisional decision to remove 23 market remedies, partially remove 4, and keep 6 in full. The remedies affect areas including retail banking, home credit, private motor insurance, soft drinks, current account switching and LPG. Interested parties can respond by 5pm on 11 September 2026; a final decision is expected in autumn 2026.

title: Strategic review of CMA markets remedies
summary: The CMA has launched a consultation to review 33 existing UK markets remedies and considers whether they should be amended or removed because circumstances may have changed. Stakeholders were invited to respond by 2 March 2026. If changes proceed, they could affect firms subject to the listed undertakings and orders.

title: Community Reinvestment Act Regulations
summary: The OCC and FDIC are proposing changes to Community Reinvestment Act regulations and related technical rules for banks, including clearer CRA consideration and reduced burden for community banks. Comments are due by 2026-10-13. This is a consultation only and does not yet change obligations.

title: Proposed steering conduct requirement for Google’s mobile platform
summary: The UK CMA is consulting on a proposed steering conduct requirement for Google’s Play Store under the digital markets regime. It would relax restrictions on how app developers inform users and steer them to offers or payments outside Google’s platform. The consultation affects developers distributing digital goods and services via the Play Store; no deadline is stated in the excerpt.

title: Proposed Establishment of the Rancho Santa Fe Viticultural Area
summary: TTB has issued a proposed rule to create the 15,827-acre Rancho Santa Fe American viticultural area in San Diego County, California, within the existing South Coast AVA. Commenters may submit feedback by 2026-10-13. If finalized, the change would affect wine labeling and appellation use for vintners operating in the area.

title: Proposed Establishment of the Llano Uplift and Hickory Sands District Viticultural Areas
summary: TTB proposes two new American viticultural areas in Texas: Llano Uplift and Hickory Sands District. It invites comments by 2026-10-13. If finalized, the rule would add new AVA boundaries and names for wine labeling and origin descriptions; no immediate obligations apply until adoption.

title: Proposed Establishment of the Mill Creek-Walla Walla Valley Viticultural Area
summary: TTB proposes to establish the Mill Creek—Walla Walla Valley American viticultural area in part 9 of the wine labeling regulations. It is a notice of proposed rulemaking for vintners and related businesses, with comments due by 2026-10-13. The proposal would affect how wines from the area may be described on labels and in advertisements if finalized.

title: Proposed Establishment of the Kaw Valley Viticultural Area
summary: TTB proposes to establish the new Kaw Valley American viticultural area in northeastern Kansas and amend its regulations accordingly. This would affect wineries, vineyards and other wine businesses that use AVA names on labels or in advertising. Comments are due by 2026-10-13.

title: Foreign Currency Gain or Loss of Controlled Foreign Corporations
summary: The IRS and Treasury have proposed regulations on foreign currency gain or loss for controlled foreign corporations’ qualified business units under section 987. The proposal would generally let a CFC elect not to compute or recognize FX gain or loss on remittances from a QBU, except for certain inbound nonrecognition transactions. Comments and hearing requests are due by 2026-11-12.

title: Proposed steering conduct requirement for Apple’s mobile platform
summary: The CMA is consulting on a proposed steering conduct requirement for Apple’s mobile platform in the UK. It would restrict Apple’s rules that limit how app developers can steer users to offers and payments outside the App Store, with interpretative notes on fees and non-discrimination. This is a consultation, so firms should review and respond by any stated consultation deadline if they are affected.

title: Proposed Removal of a Reporting Requirement for Trusts Whose Charitable Contribution Deductions Are Solely for Contributions Made by Passthrough Entities
summary: The IRS has proposed removing a Form 1041-A reporting requirement for certain trusts whose charitable deduction comes solely from contributions made by passthrough entities. It would also clarify that split-interest trusts satisfy filing obligations by filing Form 5227 instead of Form 1041-A. Comments and hearing requests are due by 2026-10-16.

title: GENIUS Act Regulations on Payment Stablecoin Issuance, Offer, and Sale
summary: Treasury proposes regulations to implement section 3 of the GENIUS Act on payment stablecoin issuance, offer and sale in the United States. The NPRM would affect permitted issuers and digital asset service providers, including limits on who may issue or sell payment stablecoins. Comments are due by 2026-10-19.

title: SEC Proposes New Regulation Crypto Assets
summary: The SEC has proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, a new offering regime for certain crypto-asset investment contracts. It would create two Securities Act registration exemptions, impose disclosure and ongoing reporting for larger offerings, and add a conditional safe harbor from the investment-contract definition. This is a proposal, not yet binding; comments are due by 2026-10-20.

title: Vets market investigation: draft Funding Order and Undertakings
summary: The CMA is consulting on a draft Funding Order for its veterinary services market investigation. The order would fund the RCVS’s activities and levy collection through payments from veterinary businesses, alongside proposed RCVS undertakings. Affected firms should review the draft and respond by the consultation deadline.

title: Determination of Target Normal Cost and Funding Target for Single-Employer Defined Benefit Plans
summary: The IRS/Treasury has proposed regulations for single-employer defined benefit pension plans that would update how target normal cost and funding target are determined under the minimum funding rules. Comments and hearing requests are due by 2026-10-19. The proposal would affect employers, administrators, participants and beneficiaries of these plans.

title: Application of Section 250(b)(3)(A)(i)(VII) to Sales or Other Dispositions of Property
summary: The IRS proposed regulations under section 250 of the Internal Revenue Code would clarify how income and gain from sales or other dispositions of intangible property and depreciable, amortizable or depletable property are excluded when calculating deduction eligible income. The proposal affects domestic corporations with foreign-derived deduction eligible income. Comments are due by 2026-10-05.

title: Application of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 to the Refunded Portion of Certain Federal Refundable Tax Credits
summary: The IRS has proposed regulations under PRWORA that would treat the refunded portion of certain federal refundable tax credits as a federal public benefit, making non-qualified aliens ineligible for that portion. The proposal affects taxpayers claiming the adoption tax credit, American opportunity tax credit, child tax credit and earned income credit. Comments are due by 2026-10-05 and a public hearing is scheduled for 2026-10-14.

title: Regulation Crypto Assets
summary: The SEC is proposing Regulation Crypto Assets, a new offering regime for certain crypto-asset investment contracts. It would add two Securities Act exemptions, disclosure and reporting requirements for issuers, and a conditional safe harbor from the investment contract definition. Comments are due by 2026-10-20. The proposal affects issuers and intermediaries involved in crypto-asset capital raising in the US.

title: Request for Comment on the Listing of Compute Derivatives Contracts
summary: The CFTC is seeking comment on a proposed approach to the listing of compute derivatives contracts on designated contract markets. Market participants may comment by 2026-10-20. This is an input-gathering proposal only; it does not itself impose new requirements.

title: Commodity Pool Operators and Commodity Trading Advisors: Reduction of Duplicative Regulation Through Intermediary Registration Exemptions; Expansion of the Exemption for Small Commodity Pools
summary: The CFTC proposes new and expanded exemptions from CPO and CTA registration, including relief for certain SEC-registered investment advisers, advisers to qualifying commodity pools, and an inflation-adjusted increase to the small pool exemption threshold. Firms that operate or advise commodity pools should assess whether they may newly qualify. Comments are due by 2026-10-05.

title: Guidance on Eligible Investments for Trump Accounts
summary: The IRS and Treasury issued proposed regulations on eligible investments for Trump accounts. The proposal would specify which mutual funds or ETFs may be held during the growth period and would apply to account beneficiaries and trustees. Comments and hearing requests are due by 2026-10-20.

title: Valuation Methodology Review for Pubs and Hotels
summary: HM Treasury has launched a call for evidence reviewing the valuation methodology for pubs and hotels for business rates in England and Wales. It seeks views from businesses, valuers and stakeholders on the current approach, with any recommended changes intended for the next revaluation. No immediate legal or compliance obligations are created by the document itself.

title: Employer Contributions to Trump Accounts and Nondiscrimination Rules for Dependent Care Assistance Programs
summary: The Treasury Department issued a correction to a previously published proposed IRS rule on employer contributions to Trump accounts and dependent care assistance program nondiscrimination rules. It changes text and formatting in the proposal and confirms the public hearing date of 2026-09-25. This is a proposal/correction only; no binding requirements are created yet.

title: Swap Execution Facility Order Book Requirement for Permitted Transactions
summary: The CFTC proposes to amend swap execution facility rules to remove the requirement that SEFs offer an order book for swap transactions not subject to the trade execution requirement. Comments are due by 2026-09-25. The proposal affects SEFs and firms using permitted swap transactions.

title: Pro Rata Share of Subpart F Income, Tested Income, or Tested Loss
summary: The IRS has issued proposed regulations on how U.S. shareholders calculate their pro rata share of subpart F income, tested income, or tested loss for controlled foreign corporations. The proposal also addresses a transition rule under the One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act. Comments and hearing requests are due by 2026-10-26.

title: Disclosure of Information; Extension of Comment Period
summary: The FDIC has extended the comment period for its proposed rule on disclosure of information. Comments on the proposal, which would update FDIC rules on confidential supervisory information, FOIA disclosures and legal-process disclosures, are now due by 2026-10-05 instead of 2026-08-31.

title: SEC Proposes Amendments to Exchange Act Rule 3a12-8 to Add European Union Debt Obligations
summary: The SEC is proposing to amend Exchange Act Rule 3a12-8 to add EU debt obligations as exempted securities for futures trading purposes. If adopted, the change would align EU debt with certain member-state debt and allow futures on EU debt to be regulated as futures under CFTC jurisdiction. Comments are due by 2026-11-02.

title: Section 898(c) Transition Rule for Allocating Foreign Taxes and Section 960(d)(4) Foreign Tax Credit Disallowance; Correction
summary: The IRS/Treasury issued a correction to proposed regulations on allocating foreign taxes under section 898(c) and disallowing foreign tax credits under section 960(d)(4). Taxpayers and affected foreign corporations may comment or request a hearing by 2026-09-17. This is a correction to a proposed rule, not a final requirement.

title: Violations of Laws or Regulations
summary: The OCC has issued a proposed rule to revise its supervisory framework for matters requiring attention related to violations of laws or regulations and for violations not handled through enforcement action or an MRA. National banks, federal savings associations, and federal branches/agencies of foreign banks may comment by 2026-10-01.

title: Proposal of Special Measure Regarding Banque Misr UAE as a Financial Institution Operating Outside of the United States of Primary Money Laundering Concern
summary: FinCEN proposes to designate Banque Misr UAE as a financial institution of primary money laundering concern and to bar U.S. correspondent banking relationships involving it. U.S. financial institutions would also need special due diligence and transaction-screening steps if the proposal is finalised. Comments are due by 2026-10-01.

title: SEC Proposes to Modernize Rules for Registered Transfer Agents
summary: The SEC is proposing to modernize the rules and forms for registered transfer agents, including amendments to registration, annual reporting, processing, recordkeeping and safeguarding rules, plus new rules and a rescission. The proposal would affect registered transfer agents and related securities processing activities. Comments are due by 2026-11-03.

title: Exemption of Debt Obligations Issued by the European Union Under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 for Purposes of Trading Futures Contracts on Those Securities
summary: The SEC is proposing to amend Rule 3a12-8 so EU debt obligations would be treated as exempted securities for futures trading purposes in the U.S. or to U.S. persons. This would align treatment with existing rules for certain EU member states. Comments are due by 2026-11-02.

title: Draft revised guidance on our approach to assessing merger efficiencies
summary: The CMA is consulting on draft revised merger efficiencies guidance, which would replace part of the Merger Assessment Guidelines. It gives more detail on when efficiencies may arise, what evidence the CMA will consider, and how merger parties should engage on efficiencies. This is relevant to firms involved in UK mergers and their advisors. Respond by the consultation deadline if you want to influence the final guidance.

title: SEC Proposes Rescission of Political Contribution Rule for Investment Advisers
summary: The SEC is proposing to rescind Advisers Act rule 206(4)-5, which restricts political contributions by investment advisers seeking government business, and to make related books-and-records amendments. Investment advisers should assess the proposal and submit comments by 2026-11-09 if they want to influence the final rule.

title: Transfer Agent Rules
summary: The SEC is proposing to modernize transfer agent rules by amending Forms TA-1 and TA-2, revising multiple Exchange Act rules, rescinding one rule, and adding new rules on compliance and restrictive legends. The proposal applies to registered transfer agents in the US. Comments are due by 2026-11-03.

title: Racial Nondiscrimination in Private Schools
summary: The IRS has proposed regulations under section 501(c)(3) to clarify that a private school is not tax-exempt if it discriminates on the basis of race, color, or national or ethnic origin in its educational, admissions, scholarship, athletic, or other policies. Comments and hearing requests are due by 2026-11-03. The proposed rules would apply to taxable years beginning after 2027-05-31.

title: Political Contributions by Certain Investment Advisers
summary: The SEC proposes to rescind the Advisers Act political contribution rule for investment advisers and to make related books-and-records amendments. The proposal is open for comment until 2026-11-09. It would affect advisers to government clients and their compliance programs if adopted.

title: Allocation and Apportionment of Deductions to Foreign Source Section 951A Category Income and Deduction Eligible Income
summary: The IRS and Treasury proposed regulations on how to allocate and apportion deductions to foreign-source section 951A category income and deduction eligible income for foreign tax credit and section 250 purposes. The proposal affects domestic corporations and taxpayers with foreign corporations. Comments and hearing requests are due by 2026-11-10.

title: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures
summary: The IRS proposes new reporting and certification rules for qualified opportunity funds and qualified opportunity zone businesses. QOFs would need to file annual information returns, furnish investor statements, and may need to revoke inadvertent certifications or voluntarily decertify. Comments are due 2026-10-16; the public hearing is on 2026-11-05.

title: Racial Nondiscrimination in Private Schools; Hearing
summary: The IRS issued a notice of proposed rulemaking and hearing on updates to tax-exempt status rules for private schools that discriminate on race, color, or national/ethnic origin. The hearing is scheduled for 2026-12-02, with speaker outlines due by 2026-11-03 and attendance requests due by 2026-11-30.

title: SEC Proposes Rescission of Shareholder Proposal Rule and Reforms to Proxy Solicitation Process
summary: The SEC proposed rescinding Rule 14a-8 and amending proxy solicitation rules under the Exchange Act, including Rule 14a-4(c), removal of annual report delivery and exempt solicitation notice requirements, and a shorter broker search period. These proposals would affect public companies and proxy voting processes; the comment period runs for 60 days after Federal Register publication.

title: Rescission of Rule 14a-8's Federal Regulation of Shareholder Proposals and Amendments to Rule 14a-4
summary: The SEC is proposing to rescind Rule 14a-8 and amend Rule 14a-4 so shareholder proposal handling would rely more on state law, company governing documents, and expanded discretionary proxy voting rules. U.S. public companies and proxy-related service providers may be affected. Comments are due by 2026-11-20; this is not yet binding.

title: Proxy Solicitation Modernization
summary: The SEC is proposing amendments to modernize proxy solicitation rules, including removing certain delivery and filing requirements and shortening the broker search period. The proposal affects registrants and other market participants in the US securities proxy process. Comments are due by 2026-11-20.

title: Privacy Act Regulations
summary: The CFTC is reopening the comment period for its proposed Privacy Act rule to exempt the CFTC-59 Insider Risk Program records system from certain Privacy Act provisions. Comments on the proposal are now due by 2026-10-01. The change affects anyone interested in the CFTC records system and privacy treatment of insider-risk records.

title: State Bank Parity
summary: The FDIC proposes to amend 12 CFR Part 331 to extend parity rules for out-of-State state banks and national banks when host State laws would not apply. The rule would affect state banks offering services in a host State, with or without a branch. Comments are due by 2026-11-23.

title: Merger Transactions
summary: The FDIC has issued a notice of proposed rulemaking to reform its merger-transaction review process under the Bank Merger Act. The proposal would change competitive-effects analysis, create a deemed-approval process for some de minimis mergers, tailor filing and processing requirements, and codify updated review factors. Comments are due by 2026-11-23.

title: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures
summary: This Treasury/IRS correction updates the comment deadline for a proposed rule on information reporting for Qualified Opportunity Zones and certification/decertification procedures for Qualified Opportunity Funds. The corrected date is October 26, 2026 instead of October 16, 2026. It affects interested market participants and firms following the proposal.

title: GXO / Wincanton merger inquiry
summary: The CMA granted derogations from an Initial Enforcement Order in the GXO/Wincanton merger inquiry, allowing limited steps such as de-listing, re-registration, board changes and insurance arrangements, subject to strict conditions. The letter applies to GXO and Wincanton and requires information-sharing and conduct limits to preserve the CMA’s investigation.

title: Suspected anti-competitive conduct in relation to hotel accommodation services
summary: The CMA announced an open Competition Act investigation into suspected anti-competitive information sharing among hotel providers, including Hilton, IHG, Marriott and CoStar. It reminds recipients of the duty to preserve relevant documents while the case is ongoing; no finding or penalties have been made. Firms should monitor developments and preserve relevant records.

title: SEC Charges Private Fund Adviser Adit Ventures Management, Its CEO and Affiliated General Partners in Alleged Fraud
summary: The SEC filed a civil complaint against Adit Ventures Management, its CEO, and affiliated general partners alleging fraud, undisclosed loans, markups, unauthorized fees, and improper pledging of client fund assets. The action concerns private fund and investment adviser conduct during 2019-2024 and includes allegations of failure to register as an investment adviser. No new compliance date is set, but the alleged conduct is already enforcement-relevant.

title: SEC Charges Toms River Trio in Connection with Alleged $47 Million Fraud Targeting Orthodox Jewish Communities
summary: The SEC filed a federal court complaint against three New Jersey defendants alleging a $47 million Ponzi-like investment fraud and unregistered broker activity. It seeks injunctions, disgorgement and civil penalties. This is a law-enforcement action, not a new rule, so it is mainly relevant for conduct, AML/fraud, and legal teams.

title: SEC Charges Boiler Room Operator and Three Entities with Defrauding Retail Investors in $74 Million Pre-IPO Investment Scam
summary: The SEC filed a complaint in federal court against Andrew Spaventa and related entities alleging a $74 million retail investor fraud involving pre-IPO fund sales, hidden fees, and unregistered brokerage activity. The action seeks court relief and is not a rule change. It applies to the named defendants and similar US market participants, with no compliance deadline stated.

title: SEC Charges Former Executives With Fraud in Connection With $1.9 Billion Collapse of Subprime Auto Lender Tricolor
summary: The SEC filed a federal complaint in the Southern District of New York alleging fraud by three former Tricolor executives in connection with nearly $1.9 billion of asset-backed securities and related warehouse lending. The complaint seeks injunctions, disgorgement, penalties and other relief. There is no compliance deadline; it is an enforcement action against individuals, not a rule change.

title: Red Driving School: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The CMA has opened a consumer protection enforcement investigation into Red Driving School in the UK over whether mandatory fees are shown in the total price at the start of the purchase process. This is an open case and no infringement has been found. No action date applies beyond the ongoing investigation and the next update expected in January 2027.

title: Trainline: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The UK CMA has opened a consumer protection enforcement investigation into Trainline’s presentation of mandatory fees for train and coach tickets, focusing on possible drip-pricing issues. This is an open case at an early evidence-gathering stage, so no infringement finding has been made yet. No action date applies yet, but the case is ongoing and the next update is expected in January 2027.

title: Virgin Atlantic: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The UK CMA has opened a consumer protection enforcement investigation into Virgin Atlantic’s presentation of mandatory fees in package holiday pricing. It concerns whether total prices are shown upfront and at purchase. No infringement has been found yet and no deadline or remedy has been set.

title: SEC: 38 Entities Feigned Legitimacy as U.S. Advisers Through False Filings to Lure Retail Investors
summary: The SEC filed an enforcement complaint against Abrdn Canada Limited alleging false and misleading Form ADV filings by an exempt reporting adviser and seeking an injunction, penalties, and a ban on filing as an ERA. The case concerns U.S. investment adviser registration/disclosure and is immediately relevant to firms using SEC and state filings. No compliance deadline is stated, but the action is active now.

title: SEC Charges San Francisco Bay Area Private Fund Executives with Multimillion Dollar Ponzi-Like Scheme
summary: The SEC filed a civil enforcement complaint against two private fund executives over an alleged Ponzi-like offering fraud that raised over $80 million from mainly retail investors. The complaint seeks permanent injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and industry bars. It is a court filing about alleged misconduct, not a new rule, and has no compliance date.

title: Mordechai Haim Ferder and Simba IL Holdings LLC, Defendants; Mordechai Haim Ferder and Edit Fintzi Ferder in Their Capacities as Trustees of the Haim Family Trust, TF 2021 Irrevocable Trust, and RF 2021 Irrevocable Trust, Relief Defendants
summary: The SEC filed an enforcement complaint against former Lugano Diamonds CEO Mordechai Ferder and related parties for alleged accounting and offering fraud, seeking injunctions, disgorgement, penalties and an officer/director bar. It is a U.S. enforcement action only; no compliance deadline is set.

title: David T. Gilchrist, Christopher Aaron Novinger, Rebecca Novinger
summary: The SEC issued an administrative order against Christopher A. Novinger barring him from association with broker-dealers, investment advisers, municipal securities dealers, municipal advisors, transfer agents and NRSROs, and from penny stock activities. The order follows consent findings tied to securities fraud and unregistered broker-dealer activity. It is effective immediately; any reapplication is subject to applicable reentry rules and conditions.

title: E.ON / OVO merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued a notice starting the statutory initial period for its merger investigation into E.ON SE’s anticipated acquisition of OVO Energy Limited. The notice says the CMA has enough information to begin its assessment and sets 28 October 2026 as the deadline to decide whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to EDF Energy Nuclear Generation Ltd by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on DESNZ’s proposed subsidy for EDF Energy Nuclear Generation Ltd to support the long-term operation of Sizewell B. It is an assessment of compliance under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party comments, but it does not itself create obligations for firms.

title: Corey Ortiz
summary: The SEC obtained a final consent judgment against Corey Ortiz over an alleged free-riding trading scheme. The order permanently enjoins him from violating U.S. securities antifraud rules, requires disgorgement, and imposes a five-year condition that he give brokers the complaint and judgment before opening an account.

title: Institutional Shareholder Services, Inc.
summary: The SEC filed a subpoena enforcement action in federal court against registered investment adviser Institutional Shareholder Services, Inc. to compel compliance with an outstanding administrative subpoena tied to an SEC examination and investigation. The case does not allege a concluded violation, but it signals an active enforcement matter for a SEC-registered adviser.

title: Parker Terrill Austin; Embarcadero Capital Advisors, Inc.
summary: The SEC filed a federal court complaint against Parker Terrill Austin and Embarcadero Capital Advisors, alleging Advisers Act violations involving misuse of client nonpublic information, fraudulent misrepresentations to clients, and false filings. The complaint seeks permanent injunctions, disgorgement, prejudgment interest and civil penalties. This is enforcement action in the United States, with no firm compliance deadline stated.

title: Omar Dario Chavez
summary: The SEC filed fraud charges against California resident Omar Dario Chavez for allegedly misleading clients, misappropriating client funds, and violating U.S. securities and investment adviser antifraud provisions. The action seeks injunctions, disgorgement, interest and civil penalties. It is an enforcement matter with no compliance deadline for firms, but it is relevant to firms offering securities or advisory services and their fraud controls.

title: Waldon Fenster
summary: The SEC filed a settled enforcement action against former investment adviser Waldon Fenster over alleged investor fraud and misappropriation of private fund assets. He consented, subject to court approval, to permanent antifraud injunctions, industry bars, disgorgement, interest and a civil penalty. This is immediate enforcement action in the US and is relevant now for firms with investment adviser or private fund activities.

title: Mark D. Hanf and Hoai-Nam Chu Phan a/k/a Nam Phan
summary: The SEC filed an enforcement action against two former private-fund executives over an alleged $80 million Ponzi-like offering fraud involving mostly retail investors. The complaint seeks injunctions, disgorgement and civil penalties, and notes a parallel criminal action. This is relevant immediately to firms offering private funds or similar products in the US.

title: Francisco Javier Sarabia
summary: The SEC filed settled enforcement charges against Francisco Javier Sarabia over an alleged Ponzi scheme that raised over $5 million from more than 350 investors. The complaint alleges antifraud and securities registration violations; if the court approves, Sarabia will be permanently enjoined and may owe disgorgement and interest. No firm action date applies, but the case is relevant to securities offering controls and financial crime risk.

title: Energy licence modification appeals 2026
summary: Cadent Gas Limited has filed a notice of appeal in the Competition and Markets Authority against GEMA’s RIIO-GD3 licence modification decision for the 1 April 2026 gas price control period. The appeal challenges the 1% ongoing efficiency challenge and the related licence conditions affecting Cadent’s allowed revenue and obligations under its gas transporter licence.

title: Justin Chen
summary: The SEC announced a final consent judgment against Justin Chen for an alleged insider trading scheme. The court permanently enjoined him from future violations and ordered disgorgement and prejudgment interest, with payment deemed satisfied by related criminal restitution and forfeiture. No firm-wide compliance deadline is set, but the case is a reminder to monitor insider trading controls.

title: Heating oil review: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The CMA opened and then advanced a consumer enforcement case on heating oil supply, securing compensation for affected customers. It also issued an open letter reminding domestic heating oil suppliers that consumer contract terms must be fair and transparent, including limits on liability and delay. No filing deadline is set, but the case and expectations are immediate for suppliers serving consumers.

title: SEC Charges Founder and His Two New Jersey-Based Companies in Alleged $16 Million Ponzi Scheme
summary: The SEC filed a federal complaint against Ernest Ossei Boateng and two New Jersey-based entities alleging a $16 million Ponzi-like scheme that targeted mainly Ghanaian-heritage Christians in New York and New Jersey. The complaint seeks injunctions, disgorgement and penalties for alleged securities and investment adviser law violations. It is a court filing, not a rule change, and creates no new compliance deadline.

title: Paul W. Jorgensen
summary: The SEC announced a final consent judgment against Paul W. Jorgensen, former Chief Revenue Officer of Doximity, for insider trading. The judgment permanently bars him from serving as an officer or director of a public company and orders payment of $490,077.54 after offsetting criminal forfeiture. This is a closed enforcement outcome, not a rule change, and does not create new obligations for firms.

title: Adam B. Rundle
summary: The SEC filed an enforcement action against Adam B. Rundle alleging a $1.5 million offering fraud involving impersonation, misrepresentations and misappropriation of investor funds. The complaint seeks injunctive relief, penalties and disgorgement. No firm action date applies, but the case signals conduct-risk and financial-crime expectations for securities activities.

title: Invesco Alpha Inc.
summary: The SEC obtained a final default judgment against Invesco Alpha Inc. for alleged misrepresentations in a Form ADV filed with the SEC. The order permanently enjoins future violations and filing Form ADV as an exempt reporting adviser, and imposes a $1,182,254 civil penalty. This is immediately relevant to advisers and firms that file SEC registration/reporting materials.

title: SEC Grants Exemptive Relief from Certain Inline XBRL Filing or Submission Requirements
summary: The SEC granted exemptive relief from Inline XBRL filing or submission requirements for portions of Form CA-1 and Form 1, Form X-17A-5 Part III, Form 17-H, and SBS entity annual compliance reports. Firms must still file these materials electronically on EDGAR, but certain structured-data tagging requirements are waived.

title: Ernest Ossei Boateng, Intercontinental Wealth Network, LLC, and I Wealth Network LP
summary: The SEC announced fraud charges against Ernest Ossei Boateng and two New Jersey companies over an alleged $16 million Ponzi scheme targeting inexperienced investors. The complaint seeks injunctions, disgorgement and penalties. This is a U.S. enforcement action, not a new rule, so firms should review sales, suitability and fraud controls immediately.

title: Paul Thomas Croft, Jonathan David Frost, Matthew William Dira
summary: The SEC filed fraud charges in U.S. federal court against three individuals over an alleged $64 million offering fraud involving promissory notes and LLC interests. One defendant also consented, subject to court approval, to permanent securities-law injunctions and monetary relief. This is an enforcement action with immediate legal and conduct-risk implications for securities activities.

title: Welltower / multiple care homes merger inquiries
summary: The CMA issued a derogation letter granting Welltower limited consent to progress disposal of five closed care homes under an Initial Enforcement Order, subject to prior CMA approval and advance notice. It also restates penalties for false or misleading information under the Enterprise Act 2002. This applies to the parties to the merger and is immediate.

title: Jon P. Kipp
summary: The SEC announced a settled insider-trading enforcement action against Jon P. Kipp, a Washington resident. The proposed final judgment would permanently enjoin alleged violations of Section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5 and impose disgorgement, interest and a civil penalty, subject to court approval. No firm compliance date applies, but the action signals enforcement risk for market abuse controls.

title: Jessica Richman and Zachary Apte
summary: The SEC announced settlements with the co-founders of uBiome in its securities-fraud case. The proposed final judgments would permanently enjoin them from violating antifraud provisions, impose three-year officer-and-director and securities-participation bars, and require $125,000 penalties each, subject to court approval. This is relevant for firms monitoring enforcement risk and conduct standards.

title: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for September 2026
summary: The OCC issued a consent order prohibiting former U.S. Bank employee Zena Montejano from participating in the affairs of insured depository institutions and related entities, after findings that she misused bank systems to steal about $329,088. The order is effective immediately and is enforceable as a final OCC prohibition order.

title: Ellen Polcari
summary: The SEC filed fraud charges against former employee Ellen Polcari for allegedly misappropriating about $1.28 million from investors in venture capital fund offerings. The complaint seeks injunctions, disgorgement, penalties and a conduct-based injunction in U.S. District Court, with no compliance date for firms stated.

title: Michael T. Christensen
summary: The SEC filed an insider trading enforcement action against Michael T. Christensen in federal court over alleged trading in PetIQ securities ahead of a private equity acquisition announcement. The complaint seeks an injunction, disgorgement and civil penalties; no compliance date applies. This is a U.S. enforcement release, not a rule or guidance document.

title: Michael Ayala; Wavemark Capital, LLC
summary: The SEC filed a settled enforcement action against Wavemark Capital and its CEO over an alleged $9.6 million fraudulent securities offering. The proposed final judgments would permanently enjoin violations of antifraud provisions and impose disgorgement, interest and a civil penalty, subject to court approval. No firm action is required unless the bank is involved in similar products, controls or counterparties.

title: SEC Censures OTC Link LLC for Repeated Compliance Failures Related to Regulation SCI
summary: The SEC instituted and settled an administrative enforcement action against OTC Link LLC for repeated failures to maintain Regulation SCI policies and procedures for its ATS. The order finds violations of SCI requirements and imposes remedial sanctions and a cease-and-desist order. It is binding on OTC Link LLC immediately upon the order.

title: Lawrence Billimek and Alan Williams
summary: SEC litigation release announcing proposed final judgments settling a front-running case against Lawrence Billimek and Alan Williams. The proposed judgments would permanently enjoin further securities-law violations and impose disgorgement and prejudgment interest, subject to court approval. No new general obligations are created for firms, but the case is relevant to market abuse controls and conduct oversight.

title: SEC Charges South Florida Resident and His Company for Alleged Investment Scheme Defrauding Law Enforcement
summary: The SEC announced charges against a South Florida resident and his company for an alleged investment scheme that defrauded law enforcement personnel. This is an enforcement press release, not a rule or guidance, so it creates no new obligations for firms. It is mainly relevant for legal, compliance and financial crime teams as background awareness.

title: Michael D. Williams and CMI Capital, LLC
summary: The SEC filed an enforcement action against Michael D. Williams and CMI Capital, LLC over an alleged fraudulent investment scheme involving false statements, misappropriation of investor funds, and securities-law violations. The defendants agreed to a bifurcated settlement subject to court approval, with proposed injunctions, disgorgement, and civil penalties. No compliance date applies, but the action is immediate and relevant to firms selling or advising on investments.

title: Manish Lachwani
summary: The SEC filed a proposed final judgment in its enforcement case against former HeadSpin CEO Manish Lachwani. It would permanently enjoin him from future securities-law violations, restrict his ability to participate in securities transactions, and impose an officer-and-director bar, subject to court approval.

title: Kristopher A. Lunsford; AKL Transport LLC; Southern Truck Leasing LLC
summary: The SEC announced a settled enforcement action against Kristopher A. Lunsford, AKL Transport LLC and Southern Truck Leasing LLC over an alleged $127 million Ponzi scheme. The proposed judgments would enjoin future securities-law violations and could include disgorgement, prejudgment interest and civil penalties, subject to court approval. No firm compliance deadline is stated.

title: Vets market investigation: draft substantive Order and Undertakings
summary: The CMA published a draft substantive order and consultation notice for its veterinary services market investigation. It would impose new requirements on veterinary businesses in the UK, including transparency, pricing, prescriptions, complaints and switching measures, and requires the RCVS to support and monitor compliance. This is a draft only, so firms should review the proposed remedies and prepare for possible implementation.

title: Formations of, Acquisitions by, and Mergers of Bank Holding Companies
summary: The Federal Reserve published a notice of bank holding company application filings seeking approval for formations, acquisitions and mergers under the BHC Act and Regulation Y. Interested persons may comment on the listed application by 2026-09-02. This affects bank holding company transaction activity in the US.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request on Export Exemption Certificate
summary: The IRS is seeking public comments on an unchanged extension of the Export Exemption Certificate information collection (Form 1363) under the Paperwork Reduction Act. Comments are due by 2026-10-02. This is a notice only and does not change any filing requirements.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request on Application for Certificate Discharging Property Subject to Estate Tax Lien
summary: The IRS is requesting public comments on an existing information collection under the Paperwork Reduction Act for estate tax lien discharge forms. It does not change the forms or create new requirements; comments are due by 2026-10-02.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request on U.S. Tax-Exempt Organization Returns and Related Forms.
summary: The IRS is seeking public comments on a Paperwork Reduction Act notice covering renewal and revision of the U.S. tax-exempt organization return information collection package, including Forms 990 series and related schedules. Comments are due by 2026-10-02. This is a notice about reporting burden, not a new rule.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
summary: The SEC announced a closed Sunshine Act meeting on August 6, 2026 to consider enforcement, litigation and examination matters. It is an informational notice only and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; ICE Clear Credit LLC; Order Approving Proposed Rule Change Relating to the Clearance of Additional Credit Default Swap Contracts
summary: The SEC approved ICE Clear Credit LLC’s rule change to clear additional CDS contracts: new SES contracts on several sovereigns and one SAS contract on Pakistan. This updates the clearing rulebook for the clearing agency and is effective on approval; no firm-specific filing deadline is stated in the notice.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Extend the Implementation Timeframe of a Recent Rule Filing
summary: IEX filed a proposed rule change with the SEC to extend the implementation timeframe for a previously approved rule filing by 30 days, moving the Trading Alert deadline to August 28, 2026. It is immediately effective as a non-controversial SRO filing, and the SEC is soliciting comments. The change affects market participants on the IEX exchange.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing, and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of, a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 14.11(e)(4) (Commodity-Based Trust Shares)
summary: The SEC has granted accelerated approval to Cboe BZX’s rule change amending its generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The changes add a 15% non-qualifying asset buffer, define digital commodity, and permit actively managed products. Market participants and listed-product teams should review the new standards and any related launch/listing criteria.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Long-Term Stock Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Designation of a Longer Period for Commission Action on a Proposed Rule Change To Amend its Rules Related to Market Makers
summary: The SEC published a notice extending its decision deadline on LTSE’s proposed rule change for a new market maker registration and Assigned Market Maker Program. The Commission will act by 2026-09-16 instead of the default 45-day deadline. This is a procedural notice only and does not itself change exchange rules.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Nasdaq General 4, Rule 1210
summary: Nasdaq has filed an immediately effective proposed rule change to shorten the retake waiting periods for failed qualification exams under General 4, Rule 1210, mirroring recent FINRA changes. The SEC is seeking comments on the filing. If adopted in practice, the new waiting periods would be 15 days after the first and second failures and 60 days after the third and later failures within two years.

title: In the Matter of Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Order Granting Petition for Review and Scheduling Filing of Statements Regarding an Order Approving, on an Accelerated Basis, a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To List and Trade Nasdaq Bitcoin Index Options
summary: The SEC issued an order granting CME's petition for review of a prior approval order allowing Nasdaq PHLX to list and trade Nasdaq Bitcoin Index options. The approval order remains stayed, and parties may file statements for or against the approval order by 2026-08-24.

title: Baillie Giffords Funds, et al.
summary: The SEC issued a notice of an exemptive application from Baillie Gifford Funds and related applicants seeking relief to launch a multi-class ETF structure combining ETF shares and mutual fund classes. It is a notice of a requested order, not a final rule or obligation, and interested persons may request a hearing by 2026-08-24.

title: Formations of, Acquisitions by, and Mergers of Bank Holding Companies
summary: The Federal Reserve published a notice inviting public comments on an application by Isabella Bank Corporation to merge with Grand River Commerce, Inc. and indirectly acquire Grand River Bank. Comments are due by 2026-09-03. This is a pending bank holding company transaction notice, not a rule or enforcement action.

title: Notice of OFAC Sanctions Action
summary: OFAC updated the SDN List by removing one person whose property is unblocked and designating additional persons subject to U.S. blocking sanctions. U.S. persons are generally prohibited from dealing with the listed persons, effective on the notice date of 2026-07-30.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request on the Burden Related to the Withholding and Information Reporting for Transfers of Partnership Interests
summary: The IRS is asking for public comments on the ongoing Paperwork Reduction Act information collection for withholding and reporting on transfers of partnership interests under IRC section 1446(f). It does not change the collection burden or create new requirements. Comments are due by 2026-10-05.

title: Financial Institution Letter: Supervisory Relief to Help Financial Institutions and Facilitate Recovery in Areas of Michigan Affected by Severe Storms, Tornadoes, and Flooding
summary: The FDIC issued supervisory relief for FDIC-supervised financial institutions in Michigan affected by severe storms, tornadoes and flooding. It is guidance on how affected banks should handle the disruption and recovery process; the publication itself does not create new binding requirements. Applies immediately to FDIC-supervised institutions in the affected areas.

title: Financial Institution Letter: FDIC Office of Supervisory Appeals Is Operational
summary: The FDIC says its new Office of Supervisory Appeals is now operational and the revised Guidelines for Appeals of Material Supervisory Determinations take effect on 2026-08-04. It applies to all FDIC-supervised financial institutions and changes the final review process for material supervisory determinations.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 17a-19 and Form X-17A-19
summary: The SEC is seeking comments on extending the existing Rule 17a-19 and Form X-17A-19 information collection. National securities exchanges and registered national securities associations would continue to file member initiation, suspension or termination notices within 5 business days; comments are due by 2026-10-05.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq ISE, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend FLEX Options Listing Rules
summary: The SEC published a notice of Nasdaq ISE’s proposed rule change to amend FLEX Options listing rules for cash-settled FLEX ETF options. It would expand eligibility for newly qualifying ETFs, add tiered treatment if an ETF later falls below thresholds, and remove the 50-ETF cap. This is a proposal, so firms can comment but no binding change is in force yet.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board; Notice of Filing of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend MSRB Rule G-27 To Exclude Certain Public Finance Activities From Term “Structuring of Public Offerings or Private Placements,” Extend the Length of the Exclusion for Non-Primary Residences From Municipal Branch Office Designation, and Make a Technical Update to the Rule's Title
summary: The MSRB has proposed amendments to Rule G-27 to exclude certain public finance activities from the term "structuring of public offerings or private placements," extend the non-primary residence exclusion from municipal branch office designation, and make a technical title update. SEC is seeking comments; if approved, the MSRB would later announce an operative date and a compliance period of 90 to 180 days after approval.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Designation of a Longer Period for Commission Action on a Proposed Change To Amend Its Rules To Extend Trading Hours for Certain Eligible Equity Options
summary: The SEC announced it is extending the deadline to act on NYSE American’s proposed rule change to lengthen trading hours for certain eligible equity options. This is not a substantive rule change; it only gives the Commission until 2026-09-20 to approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Designation of a Longer Period for Commission Action on Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change To Adopt Rule 8.23
summary: The SEC extended the deadline to act on Cboe Exchange’s proposed rule change to adopt Rule 8.23, which would codify prohibited order, quote entry and trading activity. The Commission must now approve or disapprove the proposal by 2026-09-30.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend FLEX Electronic Options Listing Rules
summary: Nasdaq PHLX filed and immediately made effective a proposed rule change to amend FLEX options listing rules for ETF-underlying equity options. It would raise liquidity thresholds for newly cash-settled FLEX ETF options, add tiered treatment if an ETF later fails eligibility on review, and remove the 50-ETF cap. The filing is open for SEC comment; the new requirements are already effective, but the notice does not give a separate compliance date.

title: Yorkville America Investment Trust and Yorkville America Equities, LLC
summary: SEC notice that Yorkville America Investment Trust and Yorkville America Equities, LLC applied for exemptive relief from certain Investment Company Act and disclosure requirements to allow subadvisory agreements to be entered into or materially amended without shareholder approval. Interested persons may request a hearing by 2026-08-25. This is a notice of an application, not the relief itself.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 2a-7
summary: The SEC seeks comment on extending the existing Paperwork Reduction Act information collection for Rule 2a-7 money market funds. The notice does not change the rule’s requirements, but it describes the recordkeeping, website disclosure, and board reporting obligations that funds already face and invites comments by 2026-10-05.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 30b1-8 and Form N-CR
summary: The SEC is seeking comments on extending the information collection for Rule 30b1-8 and Form N-CR for money market funds. It reiterates the filing timing and burden estimates, and comments are due by 2026-10-05. This is a notice about paperwork burden, not a new rule.

title: Change in Bank Control Notices; Acquisitions of Shares of a Bank or Bank Holding Company
summary: The Federal Reserve published a notice inviting comments on a Change in Bank Control Act application to acquire shares of a bank holding company and indirectly a bank. Interested persons may submit written comments by 2026-08-20. This is a notice of an application, not a rule or enforcement action.

title: Notice of OFAC Sanctions Action
summary: OFAC added one or more persons and vessels to the SDN List under Executive Order 13902. U.S. persons are generally prohibited from dealing with them and property subject to U.S. jurisdiction is blocked. The notice was issued on 2026-07-29 and published on 2026-08-05.

title: Citizens Coinage Advisory Committee Public Meeting
summary: The U.S. Mint announced a public Citizens Coinage Advisory Committee meeting on August 6, 2026 to review proposed design portfolios for a Freedom 250 Grand Prix medal program. This is an informational meeting notice only; members of the public may observe or submit comments, but no regulatory requirements are created.

title: Deregistration Under Section 8(f) of the Investment Company Act of 1940
summary: The SEC published a notice of applications for deregistration under Section 8(f) of the Investment Company Act for two closed-end funds that have liquidated. Interested persons may request a hearing by 2026-08-25; if no hearing is ordered, the SEC will grant the applications.

title: Macquarie Infrastructure Income Opportunities Fund, et al.
summary: SEC notice of an application by Macquarie-related funds and affiliates seeking exemptive relief to co-invest in portfolio companies despite restrictions on certain joint transactions. Interested persons may request a hearing by 2026-08-25. This is a notice, not a rule or order, so it creates no direct obligations yet.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing of Amendment No. 1 and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To List and Trade Nasdaq Bitcoin Index Options; Correction
summary: SEC correction notice for a previously published approval order on Nasdaq PHLX’s Bitcoin index options. It fixes the Federal Register text by adding a missing concluding paragraph; it does not change the substance of the approval or create new obligations.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; LCH SA; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change Relating to the LCH SA CDS Clear Trade Registration Fund
summary: The SEC has published notice of LCH SA’s proposed rule change to add a trade registration fund, TRF allowances, and credit tolerance to its CDS clearing rules and policy. The change would let certain trades clear even where collateral is initially insufficient, with later collateral transfer at the next collateral call. The proposal is not yet effective and implementation depends on regulatory approval; comments are being sought.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Market-Maker Tier Appointment Fees
summary: Cboe Exchange filed and the SEC published a notice of an immediately effective proposed rule change to increase Market-Maker tier appointment fees for VIX and RUT. The fee increases would apply to Market-Maker Floor Permits and EAPs. This is a market-structure fee filing for exchange members, with immediate effectiveness and a comment process.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fees Schedule
summary: The SEC is publishing a Cboe Options filing for immediate effectiveness of changes to its fees schedule. The proposal would amend transaction, permit, surcharge and discount fees, and add certain stipends and charges for products including XSP, MRUT and DJX. It is immediately effective upon filing, with the SEC seeking comments.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Cboe Bitcoin U.S. ETF Index Options (“CBTX”) and Cboe Mini Bitcoin U.S. ETF Index Options (“MBTX”) Standard Transaction Fees
summary: The SEC published notice of a Cboe Exchange proposed rule change to amend transaction fees for CBTX and MBTX options, and invited public comments. It is not yet a final rule, but the fee schedule changes would affect market participants trading these products if approved or left in effect. No filing deadline is stated in the excerpt.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change by The Options Clearing Corporation Concerning the Payment of Interest on Margin Cash
summary: The SEC is seeking comments on an OCC proposed rule change that would pay interest on margin cash and adjust related fees, policies, and safekeeping arrangements. It applies to OCC clearing members and would affect cash margin and Clearing Fund cash. No compliance date is set yet; comments are solicited on the filing.

title: Change in Bank Control Notices; Acquisitions of Shares of a Bank or Bank Holding Company
summary: The Federal Reserve published a notice of bank control applications under the Change in Bank Control Act for proposed acquisition of shares in Piper Holdings, Inc. and indirectly The Fountain Trust Company. Interested persons may comment by 2026-08-21. This is a notice, not a rule, and it affects banks and bank holding companies seeking ownership changes.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Collection Renewal; Comment Request
summary: The FDIC is seeking comment on renewal of an existing information collection for real estate lending standards under 12 CFR 365. It applies to insured state nonmember banks and state savings associations, with comments due by 2026-10-05. The notice says there is no substantive change to the collection, but the annual burden estimate falls to 52,940 hours.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Collection Renewal; Comment Request
summary: The FDIC is seeking comment on renewing three existing information collections under the Paperwork Reduction Act, including quarterly deposit insurance assessment certifications, foreign banking/investment filings, and incentive compensation guidance-related records. No substantive rule changes are proposed. Comments are due by 2026-09-08.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Intent to Extend Collection 3038-0091: Disclosure and Retention of Certain Information Relating to Cleared Swaps Customer Collateral
summary: The CFTC is seeking comment on a 60-day notice to extend an existing OMB information collection on disclosure and retention of information relating to cleared swaps customer collateral. Comments are due by 2026-10-05. This is a paperwork/collection renewal notice for swap market participants, not a new substantive rule.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Intent to Extend Collection 3038-0076: Requirements for Derivatives Clearing Organizations
summary: The CFTC is seeking public comment on extending an existing information collection for derivatives clearing organizations under OMB Control No. 3038-0076. The notice affects registered DCOs and applicants seeking DCO registration. Comments are due by 2026-10-05; no new substantive requirements are created by the notice itself.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Intent To Renew Collection 3038-0103, Ownership and Control Reports, Forms 102/102S, 40/40S, and 71 (Trader and Account Identification Reports)
summary: The CFTC is seeking public comment on renewing OMB Control No. 3038-0103 for Ownership and Control Reports and related trader/account identification forms. This is a 60-day Paperwork Reduction Act notice, not a new rule, and comments are due by 2026-10-05. The collection applies to firms subject to the CFTC’s trader and account reporting requirements.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Intent To Extend Collection 3038-0092, Customer Clearing Documentation and Timing of Acceptance for Clearing
summary: The CFTC issued a 60-day PRA notice seeking public comment on extending OMB Control No. 3038-0092 for customer clearing documentation and timing of acceptance for clearing. It does not itself change substantive rules; comments are due by 2026-10-05.

title: Notice of OFAC Sanctions Action
summary: OFAC added one or more persons to the SDN List under E.O. 14059 and E.O. 13224, blocking their U.S.-jurisdiction property and generally prohibiting U.S. persons from dealing with them. Firms must screen against the updated sanctions list immediately and stop any prohibited dealings with listed parties.

title: Berkshire Partners LLC
summary: The SEC published a notice of Berkshire Partners LLC’s application for an exemptive order allowing it to receive compensation from a government entity despite rule 206(4)-5’s two-year lookback after a covered associate political contribution. Interested parties may request a hearing by 2026-08-31. This is a notice about a requested exemption, not a rule change or enforcement action.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 35d-1 Under the Investment Company Act of 1940
summary: The SEC is seeking OMB approval to extend the information collection tied to Rule 35d-1 under the Investment Company Act, which covers fund name/80% policy notices and related recordkeeping. This is an administrative notice for investment companies and BDCs; it does not itself change the rule or create new compliance deadlines.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 15c1-7
summary: The SEC is seeking OMB review and public comment on extending the information collection associated with Rule 15c1-7 for registered broker-dealers with discretionary customer accounts. No new substantive obligations are created; comments are due by 2026-09-08.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Order Approving Proposed Rule Change by The Options Clearing Corporation To Amend Its System for Theoretical Analysis and Numerical Simulation Methodology Description To Incorporate Options Implied Interest Rates as an Additional Source of Interest Rates Inputs for Constructing the Interest Rate Discount Curve Used in Options Pricing
summary: The SEC approved an OCC rule change amending the STANS methodology description to add options-implied interest rates/box rates as an input to the discount curve used in options pricing and margin calculations. This affects OCC clearing members and the options market in the United States. No specific compliance date is stated in the excerpt, but the approval is final and binding on the OCC rulebook change.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Arca, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Modify the NYSE Arca Options Fee Schedule To Implement a Market Maker/Lead Market Maker Posting Incentive Program for Certain Non-Penny Issues
summary: The SEC published notice of an NYSE Arca proposed rule change that became immediately effective to alter options fee credits for certain non-penny issues, including a new Market Maker/Lead Market Maker posting incentive program and removal of some discounts. The fee changes were stated as effective July 28, 2026. This is a market-structure notice, not a final SEC rule.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Options Regulatory Fee (ORF)
summary: NYSE American filed an immediately effective proposed rule change to amend its Options Regulatory Fee fee schedule, including conforming text and the ORF rate in effect through 31 August 2026 and from 1 September 2026. The SEC is publishing the notice and inviting comments. The filing concerns options market participants using NYSE American and their clearing/pass-through arrangements.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSEArca, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Options Regulatory Fee (ORF)
summary: NYSE Arca filed a proposed rule change, effective immediately on filing, to amend its Options Regulatory Fee fee schedule. The filing makes non-substantive wording changes and sets the ORF rate for periods through August 31, 2026 and from September 1, 2026. Comment solicitation is open, but the change is not yet a final SEC rule.

title: Formations of, Acquisitions by, and Mergers of Bank Holding Companies
summary: The Federal Reserve Board published a notice of a bank holding company application: American Exchange Company seeks to become a bank holding company by acquiring American Exchange Bank. Interested persons may submit comments by 2026-09-08. This is an application notice, not an approval or rule change.

title: Notice of OFAC Sanctions Actions
summary: OFAC updated one SDN entry, removed one entity and two aircraft from the SDN List, and changed identifying information for one listed person under E.O. 13224. This affects sanctions screening and blocking controls for all U.S.-jurisdiction property and interests in property. Effective on publication; no action date is stated beyond the underlying OFAC update dates.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Extension: Form N-54C
summary: The SEC is seeking comments on the proposed extension of its information collection for Form N-54C, used by business development companies to withdraw election to be regulated under sections 55-65 of the Investment Company Act. This is a Paperwork Reduction Act notice only; it does not change the form or create new substantive requirements. Comments are invited on burden, utility and clarity.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Modify the NYSE American Options Fee Schedule To Amend the Manual Billable Rebate Program and Add a Credit Under the Firm Monthly Fee Cap
summary: NYSE American filed a proposed immediate fee schedule change for its options market, renaming the Manual Billable Rebate Program, replacing certain rebates with a bonus, and adding a credit under the Firm Monthly Fee Cap. The change is effective August 3, 2026 and the SEC is soliciting comments on the proposal.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Modify the NYSE American Options Fee Schedule To Remove MSCI Related Index Options From Certain Tier Discounts and Incentive Programs and Add a Break-Up Credit for Certain Executions in the Customer Best Execution (“CUBE”) Auction
summary: The SEC notice announces NYSE American’s immediately effective proposed rule change to amend its options fee schedule. It would remove MSCI-related index options from certain tier discounts and incentive programs and add an MSCI-specific break-up credit for certain CUBE auction executions, effective July 28, 2026. The filing is open for public comment.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Fixed Income Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change Regarding Regulatory Information Requests and Indemnification of Reported Data
summary: The SEC published notice of FICC’s proposed rule change, effective immediately on filing, seeking comments. FICC would require Netting Members to provide data and other information when requested for regulatory cooperation purposes and to indemnify FICC for losses from incomplete or inaccurate information. This affects FICC Netting Members and their data responses now, with comments invited by the notice period.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; CME Securities Clearing Inc.; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change To Adopt CMESC Margin Policy
summary: The SEC is soliciting comments on CMESC’s proposed rule change to adopt a Margin Policy for its SPAN 2 margin framework. The filing says the policy documents existing margin practices and governance for CMESC personnel, and does not change the approved model itself. No compliance deadline is stated; this is a consultation on a clearing agency rule change.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Equity 7, Section 122 To Remove Daily List and Fundamental Data From the Nasdaq Rulebook and Clarify How Certain Information Will Be Distributed
summary: The SEC published Nasdaq’s proposed rule change, effective immediately on filing, to amend Equity 7, Section 122. It would remove Daily List and Fundamental Data provisions from the rulebook and change how certain corporate actions information is distributed, including making some data free on NasdaqTrader.com and timing its release after issuer publication. Nasdaq will announce the implementation date later, within 90 days of the operative date.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq MRX, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Options 3, Section 1 and Options 3C, Section 4(d)
summary: Nasdaq MRX filed and immediately made effective a proposed rule change to clarify options trading hours. It would make clear that certain equity and index options may trade during extended hours, and that orders are not routable only during the Early ETH Session, not the Extended Close. This affects exchange participants trading those products now.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Extension: Form S-6, for Registration Under the Securities Act of 1933 of Unit Investment Trusts Registered on Form N-8B-2
summary: The SEC is seeking OMB renewal of the information collection for Form S-6, used by unit investment trusts to register or amend Securities Act registration statements. The notice does not change the substantive rule, but it confirms the form remains mandatory and invites comments by 2026-09-08.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 0-2 Under the Investment Company Act of 1940, General Requirements of Papers and Applications
summary: The SEC is seeking OMB approval to extend the information collection associated with Rule 0-2 under the Investment Company Act, which governs exemptive applications. The notice says electronic filing is mandatory and invites comments by 2026-09-08, but it does not create a new substantive rule. Investment company applicants should continue to follow the existing filing requirements.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 15g-2
summary: The SEC is seeking OMB extension approval for the information collection tied to Rule 15g-2 on penny stock sales by broker-dealers. It repeats the rule’s existing disclosure, waiting-period, recordkeeping, and customer-information obligations and invites comments by 2026-09-08. No new substantive requirements are created in this notice.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 31a-1
summary: The SEC is seeking OMB extension approval for the Rule 31a-1 recordkeeping information collection for registered investment companies, BDCs and certain majority-owned subsidiaries. No rule text changes are made. Public comments on the collection are due by 2026-09-08.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request on U.S. Business Income Tax Returns and Related Forms, Schedules, Attachments, and Published Guidance
summary: The IRS is seeking comments on a Paperwork Reduction Act notice for renewal and revision of the information collection covering U.S. business income tax returns and related forms, schedules, attachments and guidance. Affected entities include corporations, partnerships and S corporations. Comments are due by 2026-10-09.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request on U.S. Trust and Estate Income Tax Returns and Related Forms, Schedules, Attachments, and Published Guidance
summary: The IRS is requesting public comments on its Paperwork Reduction Act information collection for U.S. trust and estate income tax returns and related forms, schedules, attachments, and guidance. It concerns renewal of an existing collection for Form 1041 and related materials, with comments due by 2026-10-09. No new filing rule is being adopted in this notice.

title: List of Countries Requiring Cooperation With an International Boycott
summary: The US Treasury published an updated list of countries that require or may require participation in an international boycott under IRC section 999. The list names Iraq, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Yemen. This is relevant for US taxpayers and firms with US tax reporting obligations immediately on publication.

title: Financial Institution Letter: Revised Procedures for Processing Federal Deposit Insurance Applications
summary: The FDIC issued a Financial Institution Letter revising procedures for processing federal deposit insurance applications for proposed insured depository institutions. It introduces a two-phase process with a contingent authorization within 120 days and a final approval within the following 12 months, with coordination with the chartering authority and pre-opening conditions confirmed before opening.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
summary: The SEC announced a closed Sunshine Act meeting for August 13, 2026, at which it will consider injunctive actions, administrative proceedings, litigation claims, and matters relating to examinations and enforcement. No rule change or new obligation is created.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 8b-1 to 8b-5; 8b-10 to 8b-22; and 8b-25 to 8b-31
summary: The SEC issued a 60-day notice seeking OMB review and public comment on extending the information collection tied to Investment Company Act Section 8(b) rules for registration statements. It does not change the rules themselves, but it confirms the collection is mandatory and invites comments by 2026-10-09.

title: Joint Industry Plan; Order Granting Approval of the Twenty-Seventh Amendment to the National Market System Plan To Address Extraordinary Market Volatility To Establish Temporary Price Band Protections in Overnight Trading
