title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Order Approving Proposed Rule Change by the Options Clearing Corporation Concerning Amendments to Its Rules To Establish a Procedures-Based Approach for Determining Product Eligibility During Overnight or Extended Trading Sessions Utilizing Its Current ETH Risk Management Framework
summary: The SEC approved OCC’s rule change to create a procedures-based method for deciding which products can trade in overnight or extended trading sessions under OCC’s existing ETH risk framework. OCC can use the new approach for future exchange requests, and any changes to ETH procedures must still comply with OCC’s regulatory filing obligations. The notice is binding for OCC and affects products traded on U.S. listed options and certain futures markets.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; MX2 LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Fee Schedule To Adopt Transaction Fees and Rebates, Routing Fees, and Definitions
summary: MX2 LLC filed a proposed immediate-fee schedule change for its options market, adding transaction fees, rebates, routing fees, and fee-code definitions for members trading MX2 Options. The filing is effective on submission but the SEC is soliciting comments; it applies to MX2 members and routed orders, with no separate compliance date stated in the excerpt.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Modify the NYSE American Options Fee Schedule To Amend the Exchange's Port Fees
summary: NYSE American filed a proposed rule change, effective immediately, to revise its options port fees in the exchange fee schedule. The new tiered monthly charges apply to ATP Holders using Order/Quote Entry Ports, with higher fees for ports above 300. The change is already effective as of September 17, 2026, and the SEC notice solicits comments.

title: Google search publisher conduct requirement
summary: The CMA gives Google a notice setting out reporting obligations for the Publisher Conduct Requirement under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. Google must appoint a Nominated Officer, notify the CMA within the first month, and submit compliance reports in the format and content specified for each reporting period.

title: Venture capital access expanded for early-stage companies in UK
summary: HMT announced a £100 million expansion of the British Business Bank’s Investor Pathways Capital Initiative to support new venture capital funds for early-stage UK companies, with applications for the next cohort opening in autumn 2026. It is a policy/news announcement about government funding support, not a binding rule or consultation.

title: Aldi and Lidl should be subject to the same rules as major supermarkets
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI are provisionally considered Large Grocery Retailers and should be covered by the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010. Stakeholders can comment by 2026-09-07 before a final decision expected in autumn 2026.

title: Potential designation of Aldi and Lidl under the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on whether Aldi and/or Lidl should be designated as Large Grocery Retailers under the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010. Stakeholders can submit evidence by 5pm on 13 April 2026. The exercise could extend land-restriction obligations to those retailers if they are designated.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to UDX Development Company Limited by the Department for Culture Media and Sport
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on 12 August 2026 evaluating DCMS’s assessment of a proposed £400 million subsidy to UDX Development Company Limited for a theme park and resort in Bedfordshire. It is an advisory report only, with a third-party submission deadline in the administrative timetable, and does not itself create obligations for firms.

title: Google’s mobile platform
summary: The CMA has opened an initial strategic market status investigation into Google’s mobile ecosystems activities, including Android, app distribution, and Chrome/Blink on mobile devices. It is an investigation notice under the UK Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, not a final designation or rule. No immediate compliance deadline is set, but Google may receive a revised notice if scope changes.

title: Apple’s mobile platform
summary: The CMA has opened a strategic market status investigation into Apple’s mobile ecosystems under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It covers iOS, app distribution and mobile browser/browser engine activities, and may lead to SMS designation. This is a notice of investigation only, not a final decision or new rule.

title: The CMA's programme of work across mobile platforms
summary: The CMA published an update on its programme of work on Apple and Google’s mobile platforms under the UK digital markets regime. It describes past SMS designations and ongoing work on app review, app ranking, data use, interoperability, NFC access and app steering, including consultations and future expected consultations in 2026. This is an informational status update, not a binding rule or decision.

title: The CFPB to Cease Discretionary Publication of Complaint Narratives and Visualizations
summary: The CFPB says it will stop publishing unverified consumer complaint narratives and related visualizations in the Consumer Complaint Database and move previously published narratives to the FOIA Reading Room. It will continue collecting and monitoring complaints and sharing complaint data with regulators and agencies. No new compliance obligation is created.

title: Paramount / Warner Bros. Discovery merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for Paramount Skydance’s anticipated acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery and confirmed the phase 1 timetable under the Enterprise Act 2002. The initial period starts on 10 June 2026, and the CMA must decide by 7 August 2026 whether to refer the merger for phase 2.

title: CMA publishes latest monitoring update on road fuel market
summary: The CMA published a press release monitoring UK road fuel prices and Fuel Finder uptake. It says most retailers are registered and reporting, no evidence shows retailers exploited the conflict through pricing, and the CMA will keep monitoring and review pricing practices in autumn. No new obligations are created, though retailers are being contacted and compliance notices issued for registration issues.

title: Enhanced road fuel monitoring report: August 2026
summary: CMA published an enhanced monitoring report on UK road fuel prices and margins in response to the Middle East conflict, and on its Fuel Finder compliance/enforcement work. It is an informational market update, not a rule or enforcement notice, and creates no new deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School investigated for drip pricing
summary: The CMA announced investigations into Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School over possible drip pricing, asking whether mandatory fees were shown upfront to consumers. It is a press release about ongoing investigations, not a decision or rule change. The CMA says consumers could later get compensation or refunds if breaches are found, but no conclusions have been reached.

title: Veterinary services for household pets
summary: CMA-published qualitative research report on UK pet owners’ experiences of buying veterinary services. It discusses choosing and switching practices, pet healthcare plans, prescriptions, referrals, diagnostics and out-of-hours care, but does not itself create rules or obligations.

title: Vandemoortele required to sell UK plant following pastry merger investigation
summary: CMA press release announcing the final report in its phase 2 merger investigation into Vandemoortele’s acquisition of Délifrance. The CMA cleared the merger subject to divestment of a UK plant and sales operations, to preserve competition in frozen viennoiserie products. This is a competition enforcement outcome, not a rule or obligation-setting instrument.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Ryanair UK Limited by Invest Northern Ireland
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit has opened a referral on a proposed £67 million subsidy from Invest Northern Ireland to Ryanair UK Limited for an aircraft engine MRO facility in Northern Ireland. Third parties may submit comments by the deadline in the timetable; the SAU will publish a report within 30 working days. This is an information notice, not a rule or decision.

title: Treasury to call time on uncertainty for pubs and hotels
summary: HM Treasury announced a press-release-led independent review and call for evidence on how pubs and hotels are valued for business rates, with recommendations due by end-March 2027. It is an announcement of future policy work, not a binding rule. The government says changes may be implemented at the next revaluation.

title: Aramark / Entier merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Order under the Enterprise Act 2002 for the Aramark/Entier merger inquiry. Aramark, AIL, Aramark Limited and Entier must keep the businesses separate, preserve assets, staff, contracts and information barriers, and avoid integration or disposal actions during the specified period unless the CMA consents.

title: Chancellor statement on Iran sanctions
summary: Chancellor statement announcing continued UK sanctions pressure on Iran and support for further US-led action. It is a news item only and does not itself impose new requirements, deadlines or sanctions designations.

title: 5 ways drivers can save money and avoid costly mistakes as summer travel peaks
summary: CMA published a consumer news story with tips for drivers to avoid fuel and private parking costs, including checking prices, reading parking signs, keeping evidence, and appealing charges quickly. It does not create any new obligations and is aimed at motorists generally.

title: Danone / Huel merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for Danone Holdings (UK)’s anticipated acquisition of Huel Limited. It starts the CMA’s initial review period and sets the phase 2 reference decision deadline for 11 September 2026. This is a competition-law notice affecting the parties to the transaction, not a conduct rule for firms generally.

title: NRG Fleet Services / Specialist Fleet Services merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Order in the completed acquisition by NRG Fleet Services of Specialist Fleet Services, requiring the merged parties to keep the businesses separate pending the merger inquiry. It restricts integration, asset transfers, management changes, IT changes, and customer/supplier coordination from 10 August 2026 until the CMA’s proceedings are determined.

title: The Brink’s Company / NCR Atleos Corporation merger inquiry
summary: The UK CMA has published a notice confirming the merger notice for The Brink’s Company’s proposed acquisition of NCR Atleos Corporation meets statutory requirements. The CMA’s initial review period starts on 27 August 2026, and it must decide by 22 October 2026 whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation.

title: Great British Summer Savings: millions of pounds saved by families
summary: HM Treasury news story says the Great British Summer Savings scheme ends on 1 September, after publicising temporary VAT reductions on kids’ meals and attraction tickets plus free bus fares. It is an informational announcement about consumer savings and participating businesses, not a rule or supervisory action.

title: Interim Chair of National Savings and Investments appointment extended
summary: HM Treasury announced an extension of Luke Jensen’s interim chair appointment to the NS&I Board for two more months, from 1 September to 31 October 2026, while a permanent chair is appointed. The notice also references the public appointments code and NS&I’s governance role, but it does not create new obligations for firms.

title: Ministers to boost innovation in payments with new objective for Bank of England
summary: HMT announces plans to give the Bank of England a new secondary objective to support innovation in payment systems and emerging forms of digital money, including stablecoins. The objective would sit below the Bank’s financial stability objective and extend the existing innovation approach for CCPs and CSDs. No date is fixed for implementation; Parliament is expected to debate amendments in September.

title: CMA secures compensation for heating oil customers
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying suppliers of heating oil have agreed to compensate customers after cancelled orders during a price spike. Affected customers will be contacted directly; those who bought replacement oil may need to provide evidence, and the CMA says around 800 customers have already been notified.

title: UK leads way in disrupting shadowy Russian sanctions evasion network
summary: HMT and the NCA issued a press release announcing a nationwide alert on Russia’s A7 sanctions-evasion network and wider UK actions against sanctions evasion. It also says the government will raise OFSI’s maximum fine from 50% to 100% of the value of a sanctions breach, but no commencement date or draft text is provided.

title: £100 million competition to back British AI companies to fix public services
summary: HMT announced a £100 million press-release competition under the Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme to back British AI start-ups developing public-sector solutions, including NHS productivity, compute efficiency, defence and AI agent security. It is an announcement of government funding and procurement challenges, not a rule or supervisory requirement. No compliance deadline or obligation is created for banks.

title: OCC Issues Fourth Quarter 2026 and First Quarter 2027 CRA Evaluation Schedule
summary: The OCC published a schedule of upcoming CRA evaluations for named banks across multiple US states, listing the month of examination. This is an informational notice only; it does not create new requirements, but firms listed should note the planned evaluation window.

title: SEC and FDA Announce MOU to Bolster Cooperation and Ensure Market Integrity
summary: The SEC and FDA announced an MOU to improve information-sharing on FDA-regulated products and related market integrity issues. It is a cooperation arrangement, not a new rule, and it does not itself impose compliance deadlines on firms. It may matter to issuers and firms with FDA-related disclosures or products, but it is mainly informational.

title: Three Hundreds of Chiltern
summary: HMT published a news story announcing that the Chancellor appointed Sir Keir Starmer as Steward and Bailiff of the Three Hundreds of Chiltern. It is an informational appointment notice only and does not impose any regulatory obligation.

title: 12 new experts to join the CMA's inquiry panel
summary: The CMA issued a press release announcing 12 new inquiry panel appointments, effective in September and October 2026. The notice is informational only and does not change obligations for firms.

title: OCC Releases CRA Performance Evaluations for 23 National Banks and Federal Savings Associations
summary: The OCC published public Community Reinvestment Act performance evaluations for 23 national banks and federal savings associations, including Edison National Bank. The document reports the bank’s CRA ratings and supporting analysis for the period 1 Jan 2022 to 31 Dec 2024; it does not create new requirements or deadlines.

title: SEC Announces Agenda and Panelists for Roundtable on Preparations for 24-Hour Trading
summary: The SEC announced the agenda and panelists for a Sept. 17, 2026 public roundtable on preparations for 24-hour trading. The event will discuss exchange and broker-dealer readiness, surveillance, settlement, operational resilience, cybersecurity, and potential next steps, but it does not create new rules or obligations.

title: CFTC Staff Issues No-Action Position on Large Trader Reporting for Direct Participants
summary: CFTC staff announced a no-action letter allowing Electron Exchange DCM LLC to submit large trader reports on behalf of direct participants as if the contracts were exclusively self-cleared. This is a staff position, not a rule change, and applies to Electron Exchange rather than the market generally.

title: Seras / Enva (dedicated waste wood business) merger inquiry
summary: CMA publishes a merger-notice update for the anticipated acquisition by Seras Energy Ltd of G.I. Hadfield & Son Limited. It confirms the notice meets statutory requirements and states the phase 1 referral deadline, but does not impose any new obligations on firms.

title: Chancellor takes axe to delays holding back growth
summary: HM Treasury issued a press release on plans to speed up growth and investment, including support for UK unicorns, the Northern 500, new sandbox powers, and reforms to consultation and judicial review for major infrastructure projects. It is a policy announcement rather than a rule or guidance, and it does not create immediate obligations.

title: First ever Entrepreneurship Advisor appointed to the Treasury
summary: HM Treasury announced the appointment of an Entrepreneurship Adviser to the Chancellor. The adviser will provide strategic input on entrepreneurship, including access to finance, regulation, procurement, talent and innovation, through the Budget 2025 period. This is an informational appointment notice only and does not itself create obligations.

title: Chancellor John Healey's Growth Speech 2026
summary: This is a ministerial speech on the UK government’s growth agenda, fiscal discipline and industrial strategy. It signals policy direction for business investment, regulation and public finances, but does not create or change any binding requirements.

title: On track: delivering the promises of the digital markets regime
summary: CMA speech on its digital markets regime work and how it is using powers on search, app stores, cloud and AI-related business software. It discusses existing conduct requirements, commitments and ongoing work, but does not itself create new obligations or set dates.

title: Economic Secretary to the Treasury speech at UK Finance
summary: The Economic Secretary gave a speech on the UK’s push to digitalise and tokenise wholesale financial markets, highlighting the Digital Securities Sandbox, future legal changes, and work on the payments ecosystem and digital gilt issuance. It is a policy and progress update, not a rule or supervisory requirement.

title: Competition and Markets Authority
summary: CMA webpage highlighting its latest guidance, speeches, research, policy papers, and transparency publications. It is informational only and does not create new obligations. No deadlines or firm-specific requirements are stated.

title: Public procurement in the national interest: Reflections from the CMA
summary: The CMA published a speech reflecting on UK public procurement and bid rigging, and on reports recommending changes to government procurement strategy. It is informational only and does not itself change obligations for firms. No action date applies.

title: Public procurement and competition: supporting growth and innovation
summary: The CMA published a report setting out recommendations for government and public bodies on using public procurement more strategically to support growth, innovation, resilience and competition. It also highlights bid-rigging risks in UK procurement, but this publication itself is not a rule, guidance or enforcement notice and does not create obligations. No action date is stated.

title: Procurement in the national interest
summary: The CMA published two policy papers on how UK public procurement can support growth, innovation and economic security, including a call for stronger action against bid rigging through better data use. This is intelligence and advocacy only; it does not set rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Information Commissioner's Office
summary: ICO webpage listing news, research, guidance, corporate reports and consultation outcomes. The page itself does not create new obligations, but it links to data protection guidance, fee-regime proposals and other publications relevant to UK data privacy compliance.

title: Economic Secretary to the Treasury speech at UK Private Capital
summary: HM Treasury speech setting out the government’s priorities for UK private capital, including support for growth, AI, pensions reform and ongoing work on asset management and private markets. It does not itself create new rules or deadlines, but references existing and proposed reforms and invites industry engagement.

title: New members appointed to NISTA Expert Advisory Council
summary: HMT announces five new members of NISTA’s Expert Advisory Council to provide independent advice on infrastructure planning, project delivery, private finance and public service transformation. It is an informational press release only and does not create obligations or deadlines.

title: Referral of the proposed Critical Chemicals Resilience Fund subsidy scheme by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit has accepted a referral from the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade on the proposed Critical Chemicals Resilience Fund subsidy scheme. Third parties can submit comments for the SAU’s report within the timetable set out in the notice. This is a procedural notice about a review of a proposed UK subsidy scheme, not the scheme itself.

title: Heating oil suppliers: using fair terms and conditions
summary: The CMA published an open letter reminding domestic heating oil suppliers that consumer contract terms must be fair and transparent, especially where liability is limited or excluded. It is a reminder following CMA intervention over cancelled heating oil orders and voluntary compensation, with no new deadline or rule in the letter.

title: CFTC Chairman Selig and Kansas State University Announce Agenda for October 22-23 AgCon Conference in Overland Park
summary: The CFTC announced the agenda for its October 22-23, 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference in Overland Park, Kansas. The event will cover market structure, emerging markets, contract convergence, financing, data, clearing access, AI and the farm economy. It is informational only and does not create obligations.

title: Joint Readout of Principals’ Meeting of UK and U.S. Authorities Regarding Central Counterparty Resolution
summary: The CFTC and other UK and U.S. authorities issued a press release on a tabletop exercise about hypothetical CCP resolution and ongoing joint policy work. It does not create new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Monitoring of the commitments given by IAG to the European Commission in relation to its acquisition of bmi
summary: The CMA says it is monitoring IAG’s commitments to the European Commission relating to IAG’s 2012 acquisition of bmi. This is an informational notice only and does not announce a new obligation or deadline.

title: Hundreds of new officers to hunt down dirty money networks
summary: HMT and the Home Office announced a £500 million UK crackdown on money laundering, with 500 new officers across police, the NCA and CPS to target criminal networks and seize assets. It is part of the Anti-Money Laundering and Asset Recovery Strategy and highlights increased enforcement and intelligence sharing. No new legal obligations or deadlines are stated.

title: Vandemoortele / Délifrance merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for Vandemoortele’s anticipated acquisition of Délifrance and confirmed the phase 1 review timetable under the Enterprise Act 2002. The initial period starts on 13 October 2025 and the CMA’s referral deadline is 8 December 2025. This is a market/operational notice for the parties and does not impose bank compliance obligations.

title: Co-operative Group / Southern Co-operative merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an initial order under the Enterprise Act 2002 in relation to Co-operative Group’s proposed acquisition of Southern Co-operative. It restricts integration and other pre-emptive actions by CGL and Siena from 26 July 2026 while the merger reference is considered.

title: OCS / Mitie merger inquiry
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on the anticipated acquisition of Mitie Group plc by OCS Group International Limited. This is an early-stage merger notice and comment request, with comments due by 29 September 2026. It does not itself impose obligations on firms, but may be relevant to competition-law monitoring.

title: Chancellor announces Bank of England appointments
summary: HM Treasury announces three new non-executive directors for the Bank of England’s Court and the reappointment of two existing non-executive directors. The appointments take effect between September 2026 and February 2027 and are part of the Bank’s governance arrangements. No new obligations are created for firms.

title: Delivering predictable regulation in an unpredictable world
summary: The CMA Chair gave a speech setting out the authority’s commitment to a stable, predictable and more transparent regulatory approach, with better engagement and faster processes. It reiterates existing priorities around competition, consumer protection and merger review, and mentions recent work on public procurement reports, but it does not create new rules or deadlines.

title: McCormick / Unilever merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a statutory merger notice for McCormick’s anticipated acquisition of most of Unilever’s food business under the Enterprise Act 2002. The notice starts the CMA’s initial merger review period on 17 September 2026 and sets 11 November 2026 as the deadline for a phase 2 referral decision. This is relevant to firms involved in UK mergers or acquisitions.

title: SEC Issues “Innovation Exemption” to Facilitate the Trading of Tokenized NMS Stock and Request for Comment
summary: The SEC announced temporary exemptive relief for tokenized NMS stock trading on Tokenized Securities Venues and sought public comment on possible changes and next steps. It also granted a temporary dealer exemption for certain AMM liquidity providers. The relief is conditional and expires five years after publication.

title: CFTC Staff Issues No-Action Position to Providers of Passive Software
summary: CFTC staff announced a no-action position for providers of passive software. Subject to stated conditions, MPD will not recommend enforcement against such providers or relevant personnel for failing to register as an introducing broker or associated person, where they only provide and market software facilitating user trading with registered FCMs, IBs and DCMs.

title: UK’s 250th banking hub opens in Chepstow, keeping access to cash and face-to-face banking in the town
summary: HMT announces the opening of the UK’s 250th banking hub in Chepstow, highlighting continued access to cash and face-to-face banking for local residents and businesses. It is a press release about banking access and the wider plan to open 350 hubs, with no direct regulatory requirement or compliance date for firms.

title: CFTC Innovation Task Force to Host Frontier Forum Series on Innovative Financial Technologies
summary: The CFTC announced a public Frontier Forum series on innovative financial technologies, with the first forum on AI and agentic finance on 2026-10-28. It is an informational announcement and invitation for public engagement, not a rule or obligation.

title: CFTC Staff Releases Updates to FAQs Concerning Registrants and Registered Entity Activities Relating to Crypto Assets and Blockchain Technologies
summary: CFTC staff updated FAQs on registrant and registered entity activities involving crypto assets and blockchain technologies, including tokenized permitted investments and blockchain-based recordkeeping. The update is informational and aims to provide regulatory clarity for market participants; it does not itself create new requirements. No filing or compliance date is stated.

title: Rescinding Portions of Department of the Treasury Title VI Regulations To Conform More Closely With the Statutory Text and To Implement an Executive Order
summary: The Treasury Department finalised amendments to its Title VI regulations, effective 2026-08-03, removing disparate-impact liability and narrowing the rules to intentional discrimination only. The rule applies to Treasury’s federal-funding recipients and aligns Treasury’s Title VI regulations with an Executive Order and recent DOJ changes.

title: UK – U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group Summer 2026: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and U.S. Treasury published a joint statement recording the 13th UK–U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting. It summarises topics discussed and key outcomes, but does not set new rules, expectations or deadlines.

title: Google search fair ranking conduct requirement
summary: The CMA publishes interpretative notes explaining how Google must comply with its Fair Ranking Conduct Requirement for UK general search services. The notes clarify scope, non-discrimination, transparency and complaint-handling expectations, including ranking of organic results, AI search features and related search features. Google must use them for compliance reporting while the conduct requirement is in force.

title: Limits on Loans to Other Credit Unions
summary: NCUA finalizes a rule removing the federal regulation requiring credit union boards to approve and adopt written policies for loans to other credit unions. The underlying statutory lending limits still apply to federal credit unions, and federally insured state-chartered credit unions must follow any applicable NCUA or state law. The rule is effective 2026-09-08.

title: Chartering and Field of Membership for Federal Credit Unions-Interpretive Ruling and Policy Statement 08-2
summary: The NCUA rescinds IRPS 08-2 as a separate policy for federal credit unions, because the Chartering Manual now contains the current underserved-area requirements. The final rule is effective 2026-09-08 and reduces the sources FCUs must check to confirm compliance with field-of-membership rules.

title: Purchase, Sale, and Pledge Of Eligible Obligations
summary: NCUA has issued a final rule effective 2026-09-08 that streamlines 12 CFR 701.23 for federal credit unions by removing prescriptive policy requirements for purchasing, selling and pledging eligible obligations, and by deleting detailed conflicts-of-interest and compensation provisions. It also makes conforming technical changes in part 746. FCUs should update internal policies and procedures before the effective date.

title: Third-Party Servicing of Indirect Vehicle Loans
summary: NCUA has issued a final rule removing prescriptive limits on third-party servicing of indirect vehicle loans for federally insured credit unions. Credit union boards must still maintain policies and procedures to protect safety and soundness and scale activity to size and complexity. The rule is effective 2026-09-08.

title: Chartering and Field of Membership for Federal Credit Unions-Interpretive Ruling and Policy Statement 06-1
summary: NCUA rescinds Interpretive Ruling and Policy Statement 06-1 for federal credit unions because the Chartering Manual now contains the current underserved-area requirements. The rescission is effective 2026-09-08. Federal credit unions should rely on the Chartering Manual rather than IRPS 06-1 when checking field-of-membership compliance.

title: Suretyship and Guaranty; Segregated Deposit and Collateral
summary: The NCUA has issued a final rule amending 12 CFR 701.20 to remove prescriptive segregated deposit and collateral requirements for suretyship and guaranty agreements. Federally insured credit unions may design these products with more flexibility, subject to existing lending and safety-and-soundness requirements. The rule is effective 2026-09-08 and applies to FCUs and, where state law allows, FISCUs.

title: Termination of Excess Insurance Coverage
summary: NCUA has issued a final rule amending 12 CFR part 741 for federally insured credit unions. It removes the fixed 30-day advance notice requirement for terminating excess non-federal insurance coverage and instead requires notice before termination. The rule is effective 2026-09-08 and applies to all federally insured credit unions.

title: Chartering and Field of Membership for Federal Credit Unions-Interpretive Ruling and Policy Statement 10-1
summary: NCUA rescinds IRPS 10-1 as a separate policy for federal credit unions, because the Chartering Manual already contains the current chartering and field-of-membership requirements. The change does not alter substantive requirements, but it reduces the number of sources FCUs must consult. It is effective 2026-09-08.

title: Requirements for Insurance
summary: NCUA has issued a final rule effective 2026-09-08 amending Part 741 on federal share insurance requirements. For federally insured credit unions, the rule removes redundant disclosure/reporting requirements on nonmember accounts that are not covered by the Share Insurance Fund. FISCUs and other federally insured credit unions should update procedures and compliance materials by the effective date.

title: Corporate Credit Unions
summary: The NCUA issued a final rule rescinding IRPS 11-02 on corporate credit union chartering because it duplicates the Federal Corporate Credit Union Chartering Manual. The change is effective 2026-09-08 and is intended to reduce redundancy and confusion for credit unions seeking chartering guidance.

title: Credit Union Service Contracts
summary: NCUA has issued a final rule, effective 2026-09-08, that rescinds and revises parts of its incidental powers/service-contracts regulation for federal credit unions. The change removes an unnecessary regulatory provision and clarifies FCUs’ authority to enter contractual arrangements, represent other credit unions in third-party contracts, and share fixed assets.

title: Investment Company Governance Technical Amendments
summary: The SEC adopted technical amendments to Rule 0-1(a)(7) under the Investment Company Act to conform the CFR to a prior court vacatur. For registered investment companies and business development companies relying on exemptive rules, the 75% disinterested-director and disinterested-chair requirements are removed, and the governance standard reverts to a simple majority of disinterested directors. Effective 2026-08-06.

title: Backup Withholding on Third Party Network Transactions
summary: The IRS issued final regulations on backup withholding for third party network transactions, updating rules for third party settlement organizations under section 3406. The rules are effective August 10, 2026, and generally apply to payments made in calendar years beginning after December 31, 2024. Firms operating TPSOs or payment networks should update withholding and reporting processes.

title: Geographic Targeting Order Imposing Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements on Certain Financial Institutions in Minnesota
summary: FinCEN issued a Geographic Targeting Order effective 2026-08-11 requiring banks and money transmitters in Hennepin and Ramsey Counties, Minnesota to retain and report certain funds transfers of $3,000 or more through the FI Portal. It applies to covered businesses in the specified counties and adds recordkeeping and reporting steps for affected transactions.

title: British Sign Language (BSL) 5-year plan: HM Treasury
summary: HM Treasury publishes its 5-year British Sign Language plan, explaining how it will improve use of BSL in its public communications over the next 5 years. It also notes that named ministerial departments must report on how they promote or facilitate BSL and provide annual progress updates during the plan period.

title: Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting Requirement Revision
summary: FinCEN finalises changes to the Corporate Transparency Act beneficial ownership reporting rules. The rule narrows BOI reporting by exempting U.S. person beneficial owners and company applicants, and removes the need for U.S. persons to update FinCEN ID information. It is effective 2026-08-14 and affects reporting companies and U.S. persons covered by the CTA regime.

title: Establishment of the Columbia Hills Viticultural Area
summary: TTB finalizes a rule establishing the 29,387-acre Columbia Hills American viticultural area in Klickitat County, Washington, within the existing Columbia Valley AVA. The rule is effective 2026-09-16. Wine producers and labels using the new AVA name should update geographic origin references to match the codified boundary and naming rules.

title: Veterinary Services Market Investigation (Funding) Order 2026 and Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (Funding) Undertakings 2026
summary: The CMA has made a funding order and related undertakings to finance the RCVS’s role in implementing veterinary market remedies. Veterinary businesses in scope will fund the RCVS’s remedy-related activities through a levy and related collection/estimate processes, with the wider remedies package to be implemented by separate CMA orders. No exact compliance date is stated in the excerpt.

title: Financial Inclusion Committee
summary: HMT published a policy page on the Financial Inclusion Committee, including its terms of reference, membership and meeting summaries. It describes the Committee’s mission to improve access to affordable financial products and services and its role in supporting delivery of the Financial Inclusion Strategy. No new obligations, deadlines or binding requirements are created.

title: Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC final rule indefinitely stays five Iran general licenses under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, effective 2026-08-24. Transactions previously authorized for certain educational, remittance, conference, sports, academic and related services are no longer authorized. U.S.-related persons dealing with Iran should stop relying on the affected licenses immediately.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2024-25
summary: HM Treasury explains the 2024-25 Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation and its effect on Scottish Government funding. It is an explanatory policy note for Scotland, not a rule or supervisory requirement, and has no direct compliance deadline for firms.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2024-25
summary: HM Treasury explains how 2024-25 Welsh income tax outturn data will be used to reconcile Welsh Rates of Income Tax funding. It says the Welsh Government’s self-funding will rise by £129 million, block grant funding will fall by £17 million, and overall funding for 2027-28 will increase by £146 million.

title: Publication of Iran-Related Web General Licenses AA and BB
summary: OFAC published two Iran-related general licenses. GL AA authorizes certain wind-down and maintenance-of-operations transactions involving La Nivernaise De Raffinage SAS through 2026-10-23. GL BB authorizes wind-down transactions previously permitted under specified ITSR general licenses through 2026-09-08, subject to blocked-account payment requirements.

title: Publication of a Determination Issued Pursuant to Executive Order 13902.
summary: OFAC has published a sector determination under Executive Order 13902 expanding Iran sanctions to the aviation, digital asset, gold, shipping and technology sectors. It took effect on 2026-08-24 and applies to persons determined to operate in those sectors.

title: Treasury Minutes – August 2026
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports on asylum, defence, access to work, museums and Northern Powerhouse Rail. The document records government responses and intended implementation dates, but it is not itself a rule, supervisory notice, or binding obligation for firms. No direct compliance action for the bank is evident.

title: Federal Independent Dispute Resolution Operations; Correction
summary: This Treasury, Labor and HHS correcting amendment fixes typographical errors and omissions in the final Federal Independent Dispute Resolution Operations rule. It is effective on 2026-08-28, and the corrections apply from 2026-08-03, so firms already subject to the underlying rule should follow the corrected text.

title: CFTC Further Extends Compliance Date for Amendments to Form PF
summary: The CFTC and SEC have further extended the compliance date for the Form PF amendments from 1 October 2026 to 1 July 2027. This affects certain SEC-registered investment advisers to private funds, including those also registered as CPOs or CTAs. Firms in scope should track the new deadline and ongoing rulemaking on possible further changes.

title: Unsafe or Unsound Practices, Matters Requiring Attention
summary: The OCC and FDIC have issued a final rule, effective 2026-11-02, defining “unsafe or unsound practice” and revising the standards for Matters Requiring Attention and related supervisory communications. It applies to supervised institutions such as national banks, insured depository institutions, savings associations, and foreign bank branches/agencies. Firms should review supervisory response and escalation processes before the effective date.

title: Reciprocal Deposits: Implementing the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
summary: The FDIC issued an interim final rule amending brokered deposit regulations to conform to statutory changes on reciprocal deposits in section 29 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. It is effective 2026-09-01, with comments due by 2026-10-01. The rule affects insured depository institutions and clarifies the reciprocal deposit framework for compliance.

title: CFTC Issues Final Rule to Modify Clearing Requirement for Canadian Dollar- and Mexican Peso-Denominated Interest Rate Swaps
summary: The CFTC issued a final rule changing which CAD- and MXN-denominated interest rate swaps must be cleared under part 50. It removes CDOR- and TIIE-referencing swaps and adds overnight, risk-free-rate swaps, with amended compliance dates. The rule becomes effective 30 days after publication in the Federal Register.

title: Merger assessment guidelines
summary: The CMA updated its merger assessment guidelines, replacing the section on merger efficiencies. The revised guidance takes effect on 3 September 2026 and applies to merger cases where the formal phase 1 investigation starts on or after that date.

title: Form PF; Reporting Requirements for All Filers and Large Hedge Fund Advisers; Further Extension of Compliance Date
summary: The SEC and CFTC further delay the compliance date for the 2024 Form PF amendments from October 1, 2026 to July 1, 2027. The rule applies to certain SEC-registered private fund advisers, including advisers also registered as CPOs or CTAs. The extension is effective September 3, 2026.

title: Geographic Targeting Order Imposing Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements on Certain Money Services Businesses Along the Southwest Border
summary: FinCEN issued a Geographic Targeting Order for certain money services businesses along the southwest border of the United States. Covered businesses must retain and report transactions in currency of $1,000 to $10,000 and verify customer identity. It is effective 2026-09-03, with a 2026-10-03 compliance date for businesses not already covered by the March 2026 order.

title: Clearing Requirement Determination Under Section 2(h) of the Commodity Exchange Act for Interest Rate Swaps To Account for CAD and MXN Interest Rate Benchmark Transitions
summary: The CFTC has issued a final rule amending its swap clearing requirement to cover benchmark transitions for CAD and MXN interest rate swaps, replacing CDOR with CORRA and TIIE with F-TIIE. The amendments are effective 2026-10-08 and apply to swaps subject to CFTC clearing rules and DCO clearing submissions.

title: Car Loan Interest Deduction
summary: The IRS issued final regulations allowing a federal income tax deduction for certain passenger vehicle loan interest and creating related information-reporting duties for businesses receiving $600 or more of such interest from individuals. The rules are effective 2026-11-09 and apply to loans incurred after 2024-12-31, with the deduction available only for tax years beginning before 2029-01-01.

title: Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC issued a final rule staying indefinitely three Iran-related general licenses and one licensing policy under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, effective 2026-09-08. Banks and other sanctions-compliance teams must stop relying on the suspended authorisations for the listed aircraft, overflight, bunkering and emergency repair transactions. Criminal penalties may apply for willful violations.

title: Publication of Iran-Related Web General Licenses CC and DD.
summary: OFAC published two Iran-related general licenses, CC and DD, that authorize limited wind-down transactions for specified blocked persons and certain previously authorized ITSR transactions. The licenses are time-limited through September 19, 2026 and September 23, 2026, respectively, and require blocked payments to be placed into blocked, interest-bearing U.S. accounts.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 50A and 51A
summary: OFAC published Venezuela sanctions general licenses 50A and 51A, replacing prior versions and authorizing certain oil/gas-related and Venezuelan-origin minerals transactions that would otherwise be prohibited. Firms using these licenses must follow the stated conditions and reporting requirements, including reports due 10 days after the first transaction and every 90 days thereafter. Applies to persons engaging in the covered Venezuela-sanctions transactions.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 30B and 51.
summary: OFAC published Venezuela sanctions web General Licenses 30B and 51 under 31 CFR part 591. GL 30B authorizes certain port and airport operations involving the Government of Venezuela and INEA, replacing GL 30A; GL 51 authorizes certain activities involving Venezuelan-origin gold for import into, refining in, and resale/export from the U.S., subject to conditions and exclusions. Effective immediately; GL 30B is dated 2026-02-10 and GL 51 was issued 2026-03-06.

title: Publication of Nicaragua Sanctions Regulations Web General License 5
summary: OFAC published Nicaragua Sanctions Regulations General License 5, authorising wind-down transactions involving Exportadora de Metales Sociedad Anonima and related entities. The licence permits otherwise prohibited transactions only through 2026-05-16, subject to the blocked-account condition for any payments to blocked persons.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations and Illicit Drug Trade Sanctions Regulations Web General License 35
summary: OFAC published General License 35 under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations and Illicit Drug Trade Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes wind-down transactions involving specific blocked entities through 2026-05-14, subject to the stated limits and blocked-account payment requirements. Firms dealing with affected counterparties should check whether they can rely on the license before the expiry date.

title: CFTC Approves Final Rule Concerning Whistleblower Awards
summary: The CFTC approved a final rule changing whistleblower award processing, creating a 30% presumption for awards of $5 million or less subject to Commission discretion. It is aimed at whistleblower claims and will take effect 30 days after Federal Register publication. No firm action date is stated in the release itself, but the rule will soon be binding for entities within CFTC jurisdiction.

title: Expanded Examination Cycle for Certain Small Insured Depository Institutions and U.S. Branches and Agencies of Foreign Banks
summary: The OCC, Federal Reserve and FDIC issued a joint interim final rule raising the asset threshold for certain supervised institutions with less than $6 billion in assets to qualify for an 18-month on-site examination cycle. The rule also aligns examination-cycle rules for U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks. It is effective on 2026-09-14; comments close on 2026-10-14.

title: Whistleblower Award Determination
summary: The CFTC has issued a final rule amending its whistleblower award rules in Part 165 of the CEA regulations. The changes add a 30% presumption and technical corrections, aimed at improving the whistleblower claims process. The rule is effective 2026-10-16 and affects entities in CFTC-regulated derivatives markets and their compliance reporting arrangements.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee – 17 September 2026
summary: This is a communiqué from the UK Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee describing a meeting of finance ministers. It does not create or change any rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Whole of Government Accounts, 2024-25
summary: HM Treasury published the 2024-25 Whole of Government Accounts, a consolidated report on the UK public sector’s financial position and performance. It is an annual informational publication prepared under the Government Resources and Accounts Act 2000 and audited by the NAO, with no new obligations for firms or a compliance deadline.

title: Unsafe or Unsound Practices, Matters Requiring Attention; Correction
summary: The OCC and FDIC issued a final rule correction to an earlier final rule that defines “unsafe or unsound practice” and revises the supervisory framework for matters requiring attention and related communications. This publication only corrects the OCC docket number; the underlying final rule is effective 2026-11-02 and applies to OCC- and FDIC-supervised institutions.

title: Publication of Iran-Related Web General Licenses Y and Z
summary: OFAC publishes two Iran-related general licenses, Y and Z, that had already been issued on 10 and 14 July 2026 and later expired on 9 September and 12 September 2026. The licenses temporarily authorized specified wind-down, vessel, safety, environmental and cargo offloading transactions involving listed blocked persons and vessels. The publication is informational, but it reflects sanctions authorizations and exclusions for covered transactions.

title: Publication of the Democratic Republic of the Congo Sanctions Regulations Web General License 2
summary: OFAC published General License 2 under the Democratic Republic of the Congo Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions relating to agricultural commodities, medicine, medical devices, replacement parts, software updates, clinical trials, and related medical care in the DRC and Rwanda. It is a sanctions relief measure effective from July 10, 2026.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5X and 5Y
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations general licenses 5X and 5Y, authorizing certain dealings and financing related to Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% bonds on and after the stated dates. GL 5Y supersedes GL 5X, which had superseded GL 5W. Firms involved in Venezuela-related sanctions activity must apply the current licence terms immediately.

title: Publication of International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 12
summary: OFAC published General License 12 under the ICC-related sanctions regulations, authorising wind-down transactions involving specified blocked persons. The licence was effective from 18 August 2026 and expired on 17 September 2026. Firms dealing with these sanctioned persons had to ensure any permitted payments went to a blocked interest-bearing US account.

title: Sanctions Penalties Regulations
summary: OFAC has issued a final rule creating the Sanctions Penalties Regulations in 31 CFR Part 505, consolidating existing OFAC penalty and enforcement information for sanctions programs under IEEPA and the UN Participation Act. The rule is effective 2026-09-25 and makes no substantive changes to penalty provisions, but it standardises how penalty information is presented and cross-referenced.

title: Terrorism List Governments Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC finalizes a rule amending the Terrorism List Governments Sanctions Regulations effective 2026-09-25. It removes and reserves the Syria-specific general license in 31 CFR part 596 after Syria’s State Sponsor of Terrorism designation was rescinded. Sanctions teams, compliance and legal should update controls and guidance immediately.

title: Estate Tax Closing Letter User Fee Update
summary: The IRS finalizes a user-fee increase for requesting an estate tax closing letter (IRS Letter 627) from $56 to $76. The rule applies to authorized persons who request the letter and is effective 2026-10-26. Firms or individuals needing this service should update fee budgeting and procedures.

title: Semiannual Regulatory Agenda
summary: The CFPB published its semiannual regulatory agenda, outlining rulemaking and supervisory priorities it expects to consider over the next year. It does not itself change rules or impose deadlines, but signals likely future consumer-financial-services activity, including work on mortgages, small business lending and access to consumer financial information.

title: List of Rules To Be Reviewed Pursuant to the Regulatory Flexibility Act
summary: The SEC published a list of rules scheduled for Regulatory Flexibility Act review and invited public comments by 2022-08-23 on whether those rules should be continued, amended or rescinded. This is a notice of review, not a new rule. It affects SEC-regulated entities only indirectly through potential future changes.

title: Semiannual Regulatory Flexibility Agenda
summary: The Federal Reserve’s semiannual agenda lists regulatory matters it may consider over the next six months, including final-stage and long-term items. It is an informational agenda, not a rule itself, though it invites comments on some entries. No new compliance date is created by the agenda document itself.

title: List of Rules To Be Reviewed Pursuant to the Regulatory Flexibility Act
summary: The SEC published its annual RFA review list and stated that, after review, it found no rules requiring review in the next 12 months. No new requirements were created for firms; this is an administrative notice only.

title: Draft regulations: the Co-ownership Contractual Schemes (Tax) Regulations 2024
primary_functions: Legal; Regulatory change; Compliance; Prudential; Product; Ops
summary: Draft UK statutory regulations would create the tax framework for Co-ownership Contractual Schemes and Reserved Investor Funds (Contractual Scheme), including stamp duty, capital gains, SDLT, information reporting to HMRC, and penalties for non-compliance. The rules are intended to come into force on the date stated in the final instrument and apply to relevant collective investment schemes and their operators, depositaries and participants.

title: Proposal of Special Measure Against ABLV Bank, AS as a Financial Institution of Primary Money Laundering Concern; Withdrawal
summary: FinCEN withdrew its 2018 finding and proposed special measure against ABLV Bank, AS under section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act. The withdrawal took effect on 2024-09-27, meaning the proposed correspondent-account restriction against ABLV will not proceed. This is a sanctions/AML watchlist change rather than a new obligation for firms.

title: Pensions Investment Review: Unlocking the UK pensions market for growth
summary: HMT’s consultation outcome sets final policy positions for UK defined contribution workplace pensions. It will be taken forward in the forthcoming Pension Schemes Bill and includes minimum scale and investment capability requirements, a regulatory approval process for new default arrangements, and a contractual override mechanism for bulk transfers. The consultation has closed; no immediate date is given for legislation, but the government says scale transitions may run to 2035 and a review starts in 2029.

title: Registry of Supervised Nonbanks That Use Form Contracts To Impose Terms and Conditions That Seek To Waive or Limit Consumer Legal Protections; Withdrawal of Proposed Rule
summary: The CFPB is withdrawing its proposed rule that would have created a registry for most supervised nonbanks using form contracts with terms that waive or limit consumer legal protections. The proposal is withdrawn effective 2025-10-29, and the Bureau says it will take no further action on it.

title: Small business access to finance
summary: The UK government published the outcome of its closed call for evidence on small business access to debt finance, summarising 96 responses and the issues raised about lending markets, alternative finance and underserved customers. It does not create new rules or deadlines. The publication is for awareness only, mainly for lenders, small businesses and policy teams.

title: Access to Banking Services Review: Call for Evidence
summary: HM Treasury has launched a Call for Evidence for the Access to Banking Services Review on declining access to in-person banking in the UK. It invites evidence from stakeholders, including banks, consumers and SMEs, and closes on 20 July 2026. The document is informational and seeks input to inform future recommendations, not to impose new rules.

title: Unlocking business: reform driven by you
summary: HMT published a summary of responses to its Unlocking Business questionnaire on UK regulatory burdens. It reports business views on costs, delays, appeals and barriers to product launch, and says the government will use the evidence to inform future reform plans. No new obligations or deadlines are set in the document itself.

title: Investigation into Google’s ‘Privacy Sandbox’ browser changes
summary: The CMA issued a notice of intention to release previously accepted commitments in its investigation into Google’s Privacy Sandbox browser changes. It concerns an ongoing competition-law matter affecting Google and the UK digital advertising/browser market, and invites comment rather than imposing new requirements on firms.

title: Notice of Inflation Adjustments for Civil Money Penalties
summary: The FDIC published its 2022 inflation-adjusted maximum civil money penalties for FDIC-administered violations. The updated amounts apply to penalties assessed after 2022-01-15 for conduct on or after 2015-11-02. Firms supervised by the FDIC should use the revised penalty ceilings when assessing enforcement exposure.

title: Agency Information Collection Requirements; Information Collection Renewal; Comment Request; Climate Risk Range of Practice Questionnaire
summary: The OCC issued a notice seeking comments on renewal of its Paperwork Reduction Act information collection, the Climate Risk Range of Practice Questionnaire, used to study climate-risk management practices at large banks. Comments are due by 2022-03-21. The notice does not itself impose new requirements on banks.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
summary: NCUA announced an खुले public Sunshine Act Board meeting for January 27, 2022, with agenda items including inflation adjustments to civil money penalties, succession planning, supervisory priorities, and liquidity facility impacts. This is a notice of a meeting, not a rule or requirement, so there is no direct compliance deadline.

title: Agency Information Collection Requirements; Information Collection Renewal; Submission for OMB Review; OCC Guidelines Establishing Standards for Recovery Planning by Certain Large Insured National Banks, Large Insured Federal Savings Associations, and Large Insured Federal Branches
summary: The OCC is seeking public comment on renewal of its OMB information collection for recovery planning guidelines applicable to certain large insured national banks, federal savings associations and federal branches. This is a Paperwork Reduction Act notice only; comments are due by 2022-03-07.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request
summary: The CFPB is seeking comments on extending OMB approval for its existing information collection on registration of mortgage loan originators under Regulation G. Comments are due by 2022-04-11. The notice does not change the rule itself, but it relates to an existing registration and disclosure regime for covered financial institutions and their MLO employees.

title: Notice of Termination of Receiverships
summary: The FDIC announced termination of receiverships for three failed insured depository institutions, effective 2022-02-01. The notice states the receiver has been discharged and the receiverships ceased to exist as legal entities.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Succession Planning
summary: The NCUA is seeking comment on a proposed new information collection tied to succession planning for federal credit unions. FCUs would need to establish, review and update succession plans annually and maintain related records if the rule is finalized. Comments are due by 2022-04-11.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Renewal; Comment Request; Renewal Without Change of Prohibition on Correspondent Accounts for Foreign Shell Banks; Records Concerning Owners of Foreign Banks and Agents for Service of Legal Process
summary: FinCEN is seeking comments on renewal, without change, of an existing BSA information collection covering correspondent accounts for foreign shell banks and recordkeeping for foreign bank owners and U.S. agents for service of process. The notice does not change the underlying rules, but comments are due by 2022-04-11. It applies to covered financial institutions subject to the Bank Secrecy Act rules in 31 CFR chapter X.

title: Appraisal Subcommittee; Notice of Meeting
summary: The FFIEC Appraisal Subcommittee announced an open special meeting on February 23, 2022, with items including an FY22 budget amendment and a 7-hour National USPAP update course. It is an informational notice only and does not create obligations.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request
summary: The CFPB is requesting public comments on extending OMB approval for an existing information collection under Regulation O (Mortgage Assistance Relief Services). Comments are due by 2022-04-25. This is a notice about paperwork burden and recordkeeping, not a new rule.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Information Collection Renewal; Comment Request; Funding and Liquidity Risk Management
summary: The OCC is seeking comments on renewal of an existing information collection on Funding and Liquidity Risk Management under the Paperwork Reduction Act. Comments are due by 2022-04-25. The notice does not itself change requirements, but it relates to supervisory expectations for depository institutions, including banks, savings associations and credit unions.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Information Collection Renewal; Comment Request; Interagency Guidance on Asset Securitization Activities
summary: The OCC is requesting public comments on renewal of an information collection tied to Interagency Guidance on Asset Securitization Activities. It concerns banks’ paperwork burden and the continued OMB approval of the collection, with comments due by 2022-05-09. No new substantive requirements are created in this notice.

title: Agency Information Collection Requirements; Information Collection Renewals; Submission for OMB Review; Request for a Religious Exception to the COVID-19 Vaccine Requirement; and Request for a Medical Exception to the COVID-19 Vaccine Requirement
summary: The OCC is seeking public comment on renewal of two Paperwork Reduction Act information collections for religious and medical COVID-19 vaccine exception requests. Comments are due by 2022-04-28. The notice does not itself change requirements, but reflects OMB review of the forms used for federal employees.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Information Collection Renewal; Request for Comment; Identity Theft Red Flags and Address Discrepancies Under the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act of 2003
summary: The OCC asks for comment on renewing an existing Paperwork Reduction Act information collection on identity theft red flags and address discrepancies under FACTA. It does not itself change the underlying red flags requirements; comments are due by 2022-05-31.

title: Notice to All Interested Parties of Intent To Terminate Receiverships
summary: The FDIC gave notice that it intends to terminate receiverships for a list of failed banks and bank holding-related receiverships after liquidation was completed. Interested parties may submit written comments within 30 days of the notice date; termination becomes effective no sooner than 30 days after the notice.

title: Community Development Revolving Loan Fund Access for Credit Unions
summary: NCUA issued a notice of funding opportunity for 2022 CDRLF technical assistance grants for low-income designated credit unions. The notice describes available grant initiatives, eligibility, and the application process for participating credit unions, with awards subject to funding availability and NCUA discretion.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request
summary: The CFPB is seeking public comment on extending OMB approval for an existing information collection under Regulation M (Consumer Leasing Act). Comments are due by 2022-06-06. This is a PRA notice only; it does not itself change the underlying disclosure or recordkeeping rules.

title: Notice of Termination of Receiverships
summary: The FDIC announced termination of receiverships for three insured depository institutions, effective 1 April 2022. The receiverships were discharged and ceased to exist as legal entities. This is an administrative status change rather than a new rule or obligation.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
summary: CFTC announced a closed Sunshine Act meeting on April 22, 2022 to consider enforcement matters. This is a meeting notice only and does not create new obligations or deadlines.

title: Privacy Act of 1974: Systems of Records
summary: NCUA is proposing a new Privacy Act system of records for reasonable accommodations records (NCUA-25) covering applicants, employees and others seeking medical or religious accommodations. Comments are due by 2022-06-01, and the notice says the system will become effective on 2022-06-01 unless comments lead to a contrary determination. This is mainly an internal privacy and HR records notice, not a banking rule.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
summary: FDIC notice of an open Board meeting on May 5, 2022, including discussion of a memorandum and resolution on a proposed rulemaking to revise Community Reinvestment Act regulations. It is an informational notice only and does not itself change requirements.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request
summary: The CFPB requested public comment on its Paperwork Reduction Act information collection for “Section 1022 Monitoring Collections.” This is a notice seeking OMB approval for an information collection and does not itself impose new substantive requirements. Comments were due by 2022-07-05.

title: Notice of Termination of Receiverships
summary: The FDIC announced termination of receiverships for Florida Community Bank and Tennessee Commerce Bank, effective 2022-05-01. The notice states the receiver has completed winding up and liquidation, the receiverships are discharged, and they have ceased to exist as legal entities.

title: Guidelines for Appeals of Material Supervisory Determinations
summary: The FDIC revised its Guidelines for Appeals of Material Supervisory Determinations, restoring the Supervision Appeals Review Committee as the final level of review in the supervisory appeals process. The change took effect on 2022-05-17. The FDIC also requested public comment on the notice by 2022-06-21.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request
summary: The CFPB issued a notice requesting comments on extending OMB approval for an existing information collection under Regulation P (privacy of consumer financial information). It does not change the rule itself; comments are due by 2022-07-25. Applies to private-sector businesses subject to the collection requirements.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
summary: CFTC notice announcing a closed Sunshine Act meeting on May 26, 2022 to consider enforcement matters. It is informational only and does not create new obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request
summary: The CFPB requests public comments on extending OMB approval for its Consumer Complaint Intake System Company Portal Boarding Form under the Paperwork Reduction Act. Comments are due by 2022-06-23. This is an information collection notice only; it does not create new substantive obligations for firms.

title: Notice of Termination of Receiverships
summary: FDIC published notice that it terminated receiverships for eight failed insured depository institutions, effective 1 June 2022. The notice states the receiverships have been discharged and ceased to exist as legal entities. No action is required beyond awareness and any related records handling.

title: Request for Information on Climate-Related Financial Risk
summary: The CFTC issued a request for information on climate-related financial risk affecting derivatives and underlying commodity markets. It asks for public responses by 2022-08-08 to help shape possible future CFTC actions, including guidance, policy statements, regulations, or other measures. This is an information-gathering notice only and does not itself impose new requirements.

title: Mutual Savings Association Advisory Committee
summary: The OCC announced a public meeting of the Mutual Savings Association Advisory Committee on June 27, 2022. The committee will advise the OCC on possible regulatory or other changes affecting mutual savings associations. Written statements were due by June 22, 2022.

title: Request for Information Regarding Employer-Driven Debt
summary: The CFPB issued a request for information on employer-driven debt, seeking public input on debt tied to employment or contractor arrangements, including pricing, disclosures, dispute resolution, servicing and collection. Comments are due by 2022-09-07. This is not a rule, but it signals possible future CFPB action affecting employers and related lenders or service providers.

title: Request for Information Regarding Relationship Banking and Customer Service
summary: The CFPB issued a request for information seeking public comments on relationship banking and customer service at large banks and credit unions with more than $10 billion in assets and their affiliates. Comments were due by 2022-07-21. This is an information-gathering step and does not itself change requirements.

title: Energy and Environmental Markets Advisory Committee; Request for Nominations
summary: The CFTC is requesting nominations for associate members of its Energy and Environmental Markets Advisory Committee and inviting public topic suggestions for future meetings. Comments are due by 2022-07-13. This is an informational notice only and does not itself change market rules or obligations.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
summary: The CFTC announced a closed Sunshine Act meeting on July 1, 2022 to consider enforcement matters. It is an informational notice only and does not create new requirements for firms.

title: Advisory Committees Solicitation of Applications for Membership
summary: The CFPB issued a notice inviting applications for membership on its Consumer Advisory Board, Community Bank Advisory Council, Credit Union Advisory Council, and Academic Research Council. Applications were to be submitted by 2022-07-24, with selections expected in fall 2022. This is a solicitation for advisory committee members, not a new rule or supervisory requirement.

title: Notice of Termination of Receiverships
summary: The FDIC announced termination of receiverships for seven failed insured depository institutions, effective 2022-07-01. This is an administrative register/perimeter update confirming the receiverships have been closed and the receiver discharged. No new compliance action or filing deadline is imposed on firms.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request
summary: The CFPB requested public comment on extending OMB approval for an existing information collection under the Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act and its implementing Regulations J, K and L. Comments are due by 2022-08-08. This is a PRA notice about paperwork burden and utility, not a new rule.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Renewal; Comment Request; Renewal Without Change on Information Sharing Between Government Agencies and Financial Institutions
summary: FinCEN issued a notice seeking comments on renewing, without change, the existing Paperwork Reduction Act information collection tied to Bank Secrecy Act section 314(a) information-sharing requests. It does not change the underlying obligations for financial institutions to search records and report matches when FinCEN makes a request. Comments are due by 2022-09-09.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request
summary: This is a correction notice for a CFPB information collection comment request, changing the stated date from October 5, 2022 to August 8, 2022. It does not itself create substantive requirements for firms.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Collection Renewal; Comment Request; OMB No. 3064-0001; -0178
summary: The FDIC asked for comments on a proposed 30-day renewal of two existing Paperwork Reduction Act information collections: deposit insurance applications and market risk capital requirements. Affected entities include banks, savings associations, insured state nonmember banks, and state savings associations. Comments were due by 2022-08-17. No substantive rule change is proposed.

title: Minority Depository Institutions Advisory Committee
summary: The OCC announced renewal of the charter for its Minority Depository Institutions Advisory Committee for two years beginning 2022-06-23. It is an informational notice about the committee’s continued existence and purpose; it does not impose new requirements on banks.

title: Request for Information Regarding Relationship Banking and Customer Service
summary: The CFPB extended the comment period to August 22, 2022 for its request for information on relationship banking and customer service. It seeks public input on consumer access to account information from banks and credit unions with more than $10 billion in assets and their affiliates. No new substantive requirements are imposed by this notice.

title: Request for Information on Climate-Related Financial Risk
summary: The CFTC extended the comment period for its Request for Information on Climate-Related Financial Risk from 8 August 2022 to 7 October 2022. Market participants can submit comments by the extended deadline. This is a consultation-stage notice, not a final rule.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Intent To Renew Collection Number 3038-0067, Part 162-Protection of Consumer Information Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act
summary: The CFTC is seeking 60 days of public comment on renewing its information collection for Part 162 consumer information protections under the FCRA. This is not a new rule; it concerns an existing OMB-approved collection covering affiliate marketing and disposal requirements for CFTC-regulated entities. Comments are due by 2022-09-20.

title: Proposed Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request
summary: The OCC, Federal Reserve and FDIC request comments on extending, without revision, the FFIEC 102 Market Risk Regulatory Report for institutions subject to the market risk capital rule. Comments are due by 2022-08-24. No substantive reporting change is proposed, but firms in scope may wish to review the collection and respond if impacted.

title: Policy Statement on Prudent Commercial Real Estate Loan Accommodations and Workouts
summary: The OCC, FDIC and NCUA have proposed an updated interagency policy statement on prudent commercial real estate loan accommodations and workouts for supervised financial institutions. It would update existing workout guidance, add short-term loan accommodation guidance, and provide new accounting/classification examples. Comments are due by 2022-10-03.

title: Notice to All Interested Parties of Intent To Terminate Receivership
summary: The FDIC gives notice that it intends to terminate the receivership of PFF Bank and Trust, California, no sooner than 30 days after the notice date. Interested parties may submit written comments within 30 days. This is an administrative perimeter/closure notice, not a rule change, and it applies to the named receivership only.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Intent To Renew Collection 3038-0111, Margin Requirements for Uncleared Swaps for Swap Dealers and Major Swap Participants-Cross-Border Application of the Margin Requirements
summary: The CFTC published a notice seeking 60 days of public comment on renewing an existing information collection tied to its cross-border uncleared swaps margin rule for swap dealers and major swap participants. It concerns requests for comparability determinations and recordkeeping/policies for non-netting and non-segregation jurisdictions. Comments are due by 2022-10-04.

title: Renewal of the Agricultural Advisory Committee
summary: The CFTC renewed its Agricultural Advisory Committee for two years. The notice explains the committee’s remit to advise on issues affecting agricultural derivatives markets and related participants. No new obligations are created for firms.

title: Renewal of the Global Markets Advisory Committee
summary: The CFTC renewed its Global Markets Advisory Committee for two years. The committee will provide public meetings and recommendations on global markets, international standards, and the impact of foreign regulators, but the notice does not create obligations for firms. The renewal is effective from the date of renewal and runs for two years unless ended earlier.

title: Request for Information Regarding Employer-Driven Debt
summary: The CFPB issued a request for information on employer-driven debt and extended the comment period from September 7, 2022 to September 23, 2022. It invites comments from consumers, employers, financial institutions and other stakeholders, but does not itself impose new requirements.

title: Privacy Act of 1974; System of Records
