summary: This UK statutory instrument sets out recognition requirements for investment exchanges and clearing houses applying for or holding recognition orders. It also explains how those requirements may be met and confirms that exchanges and clearing houses are not limited to investments only. It applies from commencement under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provisions.

title: Charter for Budget Responsibility: autumn 2021 update
summary: HM Treasury published an updated Charter for Budget Responsibility setting out the UK government’s fiscal policy framework, debt and welfare targets, and the role of the Office for Budget Responsibility. It is a policy/update document laid before Parliament under the 2011 Act, not a new rule or consultation. No firm compliance date is set in the text.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and related technical rule changes, effective January 5, 2022. It updates filing specifications, submission types, and validations for EDGAR filers, including security-based swap entities and certain funds, with some structured-data requirements tied to later compliance dates in the underlying rules.

title: Determination Regarding Excepted Real Estate Foreign States
summary: The US Treasury, acting through CFIUS, determined that Australia and Canada qualify as excepted real estate foreign states under CFIUS real estate rules. This affects the scope of certain foreign-investment screening treatment under 31 CFR Part 802 and remains in effect absent further Committee action. No firm action date is stated.

title: Federal Reserve Bank Capital Stock
summary: The Federal Reserve finalised amendments to Regulation I to automate non-merger-related adjustments to member banks’ Federal Reserve Bank capital stock subscriptions and made related technical and conforming changes to FR 2056. The rule applies to member banks and takes effect on 2022-02-14.

title: Bulletin 2022-01: Medical Debt Collection and Consumer Reporting Requirements in Connection With the No Surprises Act
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin reminding debt collectors, consumer reporting agencies, and furnishers to follow FDCPA and FCRA requirements when collecting, furnishing, and reporting medical debt covered by the No Surprises Act. It is effective immediately as of 2022-01-20 and does not create new rules, but highlights conduct that may violate existing law.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s January 2022 Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports on defence procurement, test and trace, Crossrail, DWP fraud and error, and Greensill-related business support issues. It is a parliamentary accountability document, not a rule, consultation, or supervisory notice, and it does not create direct obligations for firms.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2022
summary: HM Treasury sets the 2022 public service pensions increase multiplier tables, confirming a 3.1% uplift from 11 April 2022 for public service pensions, preserved pensions and lump sums. It says the Pensions Increase (Review) Order is expected to be laid in March 2022.

title: Transnational Criminal Organizations Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC issued a final rule reissuing and amending the Transnational Criminal Organizations Sanctions Regulations, effective 2022-01-21. It updates the US sanctions framework implementing Executive Orders 13581 and 13863, adding interpretive guidance, definitions, general licenses and other provisions. Firms with US sanctions exposure should review screening, controls and any dealings with blocked persons or property.

title: Notification to Institutions Covered by the FDIC's Recordkeeping for Timely Deposit Insurance Determination Rule Regarding Amendments to the Deposit Insurance Coverage Rules
summary: The FDIC notified covered insured depository institutions under Part 370 that amendments to deposit insurance coverage rules for certain trust and mortgage servicing accounts will take effect on 2024-04-01. Covered institutions must have updated deposit insurance calculation, recordkeeping and IT capabilities operational by that date.

title: Review of the UK funds regime: a call for input
summary: HMT publishes a summary of responses to its call for input on the UK funds regime and sets out next steps for possible future reforms to fund taxation, fund structures and the authorisation process. It is an information-only policy paper; it does not itself change rules or impose deadlines.

title: Burundi Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC removed the Burundi Sanctions Regulations from the CFR effective 2022-02-11 after the US terminated the underlying national emergency. Firms should note the Burundi sanctions regime is no longer in force, though actions, proceedings, rights and penalties arising before 2021-11-18 remain preserved.

title: Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements for Security-Based Swap Dealers, Major Security-Based Swap Participants, and Broker-Dealers; Correction
summary: The SEC issued a technical correcting amendment to its recordkeeping and reporting requirements for security-based swap dealers, major security-based swap participants, and broker-dealers. The correction updates Form X-17A-5 Part II and Part IIC and is effective 2022-02-11. No new substantive requirements are introduced.

title: Bulletin 2022-02: Compliance Bulletin on the Electronic Fund Transfer Act's Compulsory Use Prohibition and Government Benefit Accounts
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin confirming that EFTA’s compulsory use prohibition applies to government benefit accounts. It is effective immediately for covered firms and affects how consumer accounts are required or offered in connection with government benefits.

title: Treasury Minutes – February 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to the Public Accounts Committee on several prior reports. It explains the government’s position and planned follow-up actions on topics including the Green Homes Grant Voucher Scheme, civil service efficiency, data programme management and environmental land management. It does not itself create new regulatory obligations, and no compliance date is set.

title: Bulletin 2022-03: Servicer Responsibilities in Public Service Loan Forgiveness Communications
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin and policy guidance on how student loan servicers should communicate with borrowers about Public Service Loan Forgiveness, especially the temporary PSLF Waiver. It highlights UDAAP risks and says servicers should provide complete and accurate information. The bulletin is effective March 1, 2022; borrowers had an October 31, 2022 deadline to benefit from the waiver.

title: Bulletin 2022-04: Mitigating Harm From Repossession of Automobiles
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin, effective 2022-03-03, warning auto loan lenders, servicers and their service providers that repossession practices may violate UDAAP standards under the Dodd-Frank Act. It highlights scenarios such as wrongful repossession, deceptive or unfair conduct, and related debt collection issues. Firms involved in auto repossessions should review servicing, collections and vendor controls immediately.

title: Expansion of the Clarksburg Viticultural Area
summary: TTB finalises a rule expanding the Clarksburg American Viticultural Area in California by about 27,945 acres. The change updates the codified AVA boundary in 27 CFR part 9 and is effective 2022-04-08. It affects wine producers and label users that reference the Clarksburg AVA.

title: Import Restrictions Imposed on Categories of Archaeological and Ethnological Material of Nigeria
summary: U.S. CBP and Treasury impose immediate import restrictions on specified archaeological and ethnological material from Nigeria, effective 2022-03-17. Imports of listed items are restricted unless the statutory conditions in the customs regulations are met. This affects importers and customs operations handling cultural property.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting - December 2021
summary: Record of a December 2021 meeting between HM Treasury and the FCA about the FCA’s annual Perimeter Report. It is a summary publication only; it does not change the regulatory perimeter, obligations, or deadlines for firms.

title: Spring Statement 2022: documents
summary: UK Spring Statement 2022 is a budget/policy document setting out fiscal and tax measures, including changes to National Insurance thresholds, fuel duty, VAT relief for energy-saving materials, and business support. It is aimed at the UK economy broadly and does not itself create direct regulatory obligations for financial firms.

title: Debt management report 2022 to 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s annual debt management report for 2022-23 describes the government’s borrowing plans, debt management framework, and the remit for the Debt Management Office, NS&I and Exchequer cash management. It is informational and sets out policy context rather than creating new obligations for firms. Relevant mainly for market awareness and sovereign debt/liquidity monitoring.

title: National Insurance Contributions (Increase of Thresholds) Bill
summary: Draft UK Bill to raise National Insurance contribution thresholds for Class 1, 2 and 4 contributions. It changes threshold amounts in social security legislation, with some changes effective from 6 April 2022 and 6 July 2022, and requires Treasury regulations to align Class 2 thresholds with Class 4. It affects UK employers and self-employed contributors.

title: Income Taxes
summary: The IRS published a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 1, removing specified erroneous paragraphs from section 1.263A-3 in the annual income tax regulations revision. This is a technical codification update for affected taxpayers, effective on publication, with no new substantive rule content.

title: Income Taxes
summary: The IRS/Federal Register issued a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 1, fixing editorial/technical errors in the income tax rule on stock basis in certain triangular reorganizations. It clarifies the applicability dates in § 1.358-6 for reorganizations occurring on or after specified historic dates.

title: Income Taxes
summary: This IRS CFR correction republishes 26 CFR Part 1 to fix an editorial/technical error in § 1.351-3 on records and filing requirements. It restates the effective/applicability dates for taxpayers and applies to taxable years beginning on or after May 30, 2006, with specific exchange-date rules for paragraphs (a)(3) and (b)(3).

title: Income Taxes
summary: The IRS published a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 1, fixing technical errors in the income tax regulations for certain modified guaranteed contracts. The correction states the applicable dates for section 1.817A-1 and removes an obsolete paragraph in section 1.818-2. It applies to taxable years beginning after October 13, 2020, with a limited taxpayer election back to years after December 31, 2017.

title: Income Taxes
summary: The IRS published a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 1 on excess deductions when an estate or trust terminates. It corrects the text of the rule for beneficiaries claiming deductions in the termination year. Applies to estates, trusts and beneficiaries; effective as a code correction on publication.

title: Treasury Minutes –  7 April 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to Committee of Public Accounts reports on several public-sector topics, including gigabit broadband, state pension underpayments, local government finance and NHS payment schemes. It records agreed actions and target implementation dates for the named departments, but does not itself create bank-specific regulatory obligations.

title: Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 121
summary: The SEC staff issued Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 121, effective 2022-04-11, giving interpretive accounting guidance for entities that safeguard crypto-assets held for platform users. It applies to SEC reporting companies, entities with pending SEC registration statements, Regulation A filers, and certain SPAC-related businesses. Firms in scope should assess recognition, measurement and disclosure treatment for these arrangements.

title: World Bank Spring Meetings 2022: UK Governor’s statement
summary: The UK Governor’s statement to the World Bank Spring Meetings calls on the World Bank, IMF and international community to provide additional support for Ukraine, neighbouring countries and developing economies. It is a policy statement with no direct obligations or compliance deadline for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – 26 April 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to PAC recommendations across several public-spending and operational reports, including EU Exit border planning and HMRC performance. It asks departments to implement or report back on specific actions, with some target dates through October 2022, Winter 2023 and Spring 2023. This is an accountability/expectations document, not a rule change.

title: Liquidity Risk Measurement Standards
summary: The FDIC published a CFR correction to 12 CFR part 329 (Liquidity Risk Measurement Standards). It fixes technical text in sections 329.22 and 329.40 and applies to FDIC-supervised institutions. No substantive policy change is described, but the corrected rule text is part of the current handbook/rulebook.

title: Terms of engagement between HM Treasury and Pool Reinsurance Limited (Pool Re)
summary: HM Treasury and Pool Re issued an updated framework agreement setting out Pool Re’s governance, accountability, reporting, audit and financial arrangements. It applies to Pool Re and its ONS-classified subsidiaries/joint ventures and confirms how the relationship with HM Treasury should operate. The document is effective from May 2022 and should be reviewed periodically, but it does not itself create new legal powers.

title: Publication of Ukraine-/Russia-Related Web General Licenses 13Q and 13R
summary: OFAC published updated Ukraine-/Russia-related general licenses 13Q and 13R for divestment or transfer of certain GAZ Group-related holdings and related settlement activity. U.S. persons using the license must file a detailed transaction report within 10 business days after the license expires. The licenses were time-limited and 13R expired on May 25, 2022.

title: Loans in Areas Having Special Flood Hazards; Interagency Questions and Answers Regarding Flood Insurance
summary: The OCC and other federal agencies issued revised interagency flood insurance Q&As to help lenders comply with Federal flood insurance law. The guidance updates expectations on escrow of premiums, detached structure exemptions, force placement and acceptance of private flood insurance. It is effective from the issuance date of 2022-05-11 and applies to federally regulated lending institutions and related lenders.

title: Publication of Financial Services Sectoral Determination and Directives 1A, 2, 3, and 4 Under Executive Order 14024 of April 15, 2021
summary: OFAC published the Financial Services Sectoral Determination and Directives 1A, 2, 3 and 4 under Executive Order 14024, making Russia-related sanctions on financial services, sovereign debt, correspondent accounts, new debt/equity, and certain Russian state entities immediately effective or effective from specified March 2022 dates. U.S. persons and financial institutions must ensure sanctions screening and transaction restrictions are in place.

title: Establishment of the Rocky Reach Viticultural Area
summary: TTB establishes the new Rocky Reach American viticultural area in Washington state, within the existing Columbia Valley AVA. The rule is effective 2022-07-05 and affects wine labeling/origin descriptions for vintners using grapes from the area.

title: Establishment of the Upper Lake Valley Viticultural Area and Modification of the Clear Lake Viticultural Area
summary: TTB finalises a codified wine-label rule establishing the Upper Lake Valley viticultural area in California and expanding the existing Clear Lake viticultural area so it fully contains it. The rule is effective 2022-07-05. It affects wine producers and label users in the named area and updates the AVA boundaries in 27 CFR part 9.

title: Critical third parties to the finance sector: policy statement
summary: HM Treasury sets out its policy proposal for a regime to designate certain finance-sector third parties as critical and let regulators oversee their material services. The statement explains the rationale and intended powers but does not itself create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Fees for Reviews of the Rule Enforcement Programs of Designated Contract Markets and Registered Futures Associations
summary: The CFTC set the 2021 fee schedule for reviews of rule enforcement programs at designated contract markets and registered futures associations. Each self-regulatory organization must remit the applicable fee electronically by 2022-08-16. The notice applies to DCMs and the National Futures Association and is based on the CFTC’s cost-recovery methodology.

title: Independent Report preceding the Fiscal Framework review: terms of reference
summary: HM Treasury published terms of reference for an independent report preceding the Fiscal Framework review. It is an information paper setting out the scope of the review, with no direct requirements, deadlines, or compliance actions for firms.

title: Debt Collection Practices (Regulation F); Pay-to-Pay Fees
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion under Regulation F stating that debt collectors may not collect pay-to-pay or convenience fees unless the debt agreement or law expressly authorizes them, including when fees are collected through a third-party processor. It is effective immediately from 2022-07-05 and applies to debt collectors subject to the FDCPA/Regulation F.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2020-21
summary: HMT explains the 2020-21 Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation and its effect on Welsh Government funding for 2023-24. It is an explanatory policy paper, not a rule, and it does not create obligations for firms.

title: National Insurance Fund Investment Account Report & Accounts 2021 to 2022
summary: This is the UK government’s annual report and accounts for the National Insurance Fund Investment Account for the year ended 31 March 2022. It explains the fund’s investment activity, performance, and audited accounts, and is laid before Parliament. It does not create new requirements for banks or other regulated firms.

title: Fees for Reviews of the Rule Enforcement Programs of Designated Contract Markets and Registered Futures Associations; Correction
summary: The CFTC corrected the 2021 schedule of fees for reviews of rule enforcement programs for designated contract markets and registered futures associations. Self-regulatory organizations must remit the applicable fee electronically by 2022-08-16. The correction fixes assessed fee data in Table 2 from the June 17, 2022 Federal Register notice.

title: Fair Credit Reporting; Permissible Purposes for Furnishing, Using, and Obtaining Consumer Reports
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion under FCRA section 604 on permissible purposes for consumer reports. It says a consumer reporting agency may provide a report only if it has reason to believe all information pertains to the consumer requested, and disclaimers do not fix a missing permissible purpose. Effective July 12, 2022. Applies to consumer reporting agencies and consumer report users in the US.

title: Levelling Up Fund Round 2: prospectus
summary: This policy paper sets out guidance for local authorities and certain local applicants on how to bid for Round 2 of the UK Levelling Up Fund. It is informational only and does not itself create regulatory obligations for banks. The fund runs until 2024/25.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) – 27 June 2022
summary: This is a UK government policy communiqué on discussions between the UK and Scottish governments about the upcoming review of the Scottish Government’s fiscal framework. It reports talks only and does not create or change obligations, deadlines, or rules.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and Rule 301, effective 2022-07-19. The changes reflect recent EDGAR system releases, new filing submission type SPDSCL for HFCAA-related submissions, and updated filing fee payment methods. Filers using EDGAR, including issuers and other registrants, must follow the revised manual for electronic submissions.

title: Finance Bill 2021-2022: Report Stage
summary: UK Finance (No. 2) Bill report stage materials set out amendments to the new qualifying asset holding company regime, including technical fixes, definitions and clarifications to the tax rules. This is relevant to firms using or structuring QAHCs and investment vehicles in the UK. No filing date is given in this extract.

title: Departmental Minute from HM Treasury: UK Infrastructure Bank Guarantees
summary: HM Treasury published a departmental minute notifying Parliament that it intends to create a contingent liability for up to £10 billion of UK Infrastructure Bank guarantees to support infrastructure investment, climate goals and regional growth. It is a notice of intent, not a rule or obligation, and no action or deadline is set for firms.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 39, 40, 41, 42, and 43
summary: OFAC published five Russian sanctions general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize specified wind-down, civil aviation safety, and other transactions involving named blocked parties, with some expiring on stated dates and others with no expiry. Firms dealing with Russia-linked persons, goods or services must check whether their activity is covered and by when.

title: Treasury minutes - August 2022
summary: Treasury Minutes records the UK government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports, including IR35 tax reform, evaluation and modelling, local growth, DHSC accounts, Ajax, and higher education. It sets out agreed actions and target implementation dates such as December 2022, March 2023 and December 2023, but it does not itself create new rules.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8I and 8J
summary: OFAC published Venezuela General Licenses 8I and 8J under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. GL 8J supersedes the expired GL 8I and authorizes certain PdVSA-related transactions for named covered entities until 2022-12-01, subject to detailed limits. Sanctions teams and operations need to apply the current licence conditions; other Venezuela prohibitions remain in force.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 6, 6A, 6B, 25C, 30A, and 44
summary: OFAC published six web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions involving agricultural commodities, medicine, medical devices, COVID-19 activities and related clinical trials. The licenses were previously issued on OFAC’s website; GL 30A expires on 2022-12-16 while the others have no stated expiry. Firms dealing with Russia-related sanctioned activity should check the scope before relying on them.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 40 and 40A
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 40A, replacing expired GL 40. The license authorizes certain liquefied petroleum gas export/reexport transactions involving the Government of Venezuela or PdVSA through 2023-07-12, subject to stated exclusions. Firms dealing with Venezuela-related sanctions matters should confirm whether their activity falls within the authorization and update sanctions controls accordingly.

title: Government response to the National Infrastructure Commission report Infrastructure, Towns and Regeneration
summary: Government policy paper responding to the National Infrastructure Commission’s report on infrastructure, towns and regeneration in England. It discusses how the government intends to respond to recommendations on transport and digital infrastructure, but it does not create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-04: Insufficient Data Protection or Security for Sensitive Consumer Information
summary: The CFPB issued a circular stating that inadequate data protection or information security for sensitive consumer information can be an unfair act or practice under the CFPA, even without an actual breach. It highlights weak authentication, password management and software update controls as risky for covered persons and service providers. No new deadline is set, but firms should assess controls now.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 38A and 50
summary: OFAC published two Russia-related general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 38A authorizes certain pension-payment transactions and replaces GL 38, while GL 50 authorizes closing individual accounts at blocked financial institutions and transferring remaining funds, subject to limits. Effective 2022-08-19; no expiry date is stated.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 14, 15, 16, 17, 17A, 18, 19, and 20
summary: OFAC published eight general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize or carve out certain Russia-related transactions, including clearing and settlement activity, dealings with certain blocked Usmanov entities, and limited imports of specified Russian-origin energy and coal products under pre-existing contracts, subject to stated conditions and expirations.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-05: Debt Collection and Consumer Reporting Practices Involving Invalid Nursing Home Debts
summary: The CFPB issued a circular explaining that debt collection and consumer reporting practices tied to nursing home debts invalid under the Nursing Home Reform Act can violate the FDCPA and FCRA. It does not itself create new requirements, but signals enforcement risk for firms involved in collecting or furnishing information on such debts.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: documents
summary: HM Treasury’s Growth Plan 2022 is a policy paper setting out the government’s economic and tax agenda, including energy support, investment zones and planned tax cuts. It is primarily informational for firms and does not itself create binding regulatory requirements, though it signals future tax and market policy changes. No firm-specific action date is stated in the document excerpt.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Income Tax
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet explaining the Chancellor’s announced changes to the Basic and Additional Rates of Income Tax in the Growth Plan 2022. It is an informational policy paper only and does not itself create or change obligations for firms. No action date is set in the document.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations and Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8 and 8A
summary: OFAC published two general licenses under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations and Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations. GL 8 and GL 8A authorize certain humanitarian trade transactions involving the Central Bank of Iran, and GL 8A also covers the National Iranian Oil Company and entities it controls. Firms dealing in sanctioned goods or payments must check the scope and limits of the licenses immediately.

title: Statement on Competition and Innovation
summary: The CFPB rescinds its No-Action Letter Policy and Compliance Assistance Sandbox Policy, effective 2022-09-30, because the PRA authorization expired and will not be renewed. Firms can no longer submit new applications under those policies from that date, though Trial Disclosure Policy requests continue to be accepted and existing submissions will be notified of any further action.

title: Central African Republic Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC has finalized and reissued the Central African Republic Sanctions Regulations, effective 2022-09-29. The rule updates the consolidated sanctions text with additional definitions, interpretive guidance, general licenses and other provisions for persons subject to U.S. sanctions compliance requirements.

title: Regulation Crowdfunding, General Rules and Regulations
summary: This CFR correction updates Regulation Crowdfunding disclosure rules in 17 CFR Part 227 by adding a paragraph to § 227.201. It applies to issuers using Regulation Crowdfunding and affects written communications and broadcast scripts covered by the rule. The correction is effective as published in the CFR correction notice.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and related Rule 301 amendments, effective 2022-10-13. The update aligns filing instructions and submission types with prior EDGAR system releases and electronic-filing requirements, including Form 13F confidential treatment requests, certain Advisers Act applications, and Form 144 electronic filing. Filers subject to SEC electronic submission rules should use the updated manual immediately.

title: Joint Statement: UK – U.S. Covered Agreement. Second meeting on the Joint Committee
summary: HM Treasury, the US Treasury and the USTR issued a joint statement on the second meeting of the UK-U.S. Covered Agreement Joint Committee. It summarises discussion topics between the two governments on prudential measures for insurance and reinsurance; it does not create new obligations or deadlines.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-06: Unanticipated Overdraft Fee Assessment Practices
summary: The CFPB issued Circular 2022-06 stating that unanticipated overdraft fee practices can be unfair under the CFPA even where a firm complies with TILA, EFTA, Regulation Z and Regulation E. Banks and credit unions offering overdraft programs should review fee assessment practices, especially APSN-style transactions, for alignment with UDAAP expectations.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: documents
summary: This is the UK Autumn Statement 2022, a government fiscal policy and economic update. It announces tax and spending measures, including changes affecting business taxation and public spending, but it is not itself a regulatory rule, supervisory notice, or binding obligation for firms.

title: Terms of Reference: Review of the Energy Bill Relief Scheme
summary: HM Treasury publishes terms of reference for a review of the Energy Bill Relief Scheme, setting out the review’s context, scope, governance and timetable for reporting. It does not create or change obligations for firms.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: Cost of living support Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury’s factsheet explains the Autumn Statement 2022 cost-of-living support for households, including income support, energy bill help, benefits uprating, and tax and wage changes. It is informational only and does not itself create obligations for firms.

title: Minutes of the Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes: 6 October 2022
summary: HMT published minutes of the UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes, describing the committee’s meeting under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It is informational only and does not itself change VAT, tax recovery, or fraud-cooperation requirements.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on the United Kingdom-Singapore FinTech Bridge
summary: The UK and Singapore signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen cooperation on FinTech policy, regulator-to-regulator engagement, and business-to-business support. It sets out quarterly discussions, sharing of FinTech developments, and possible joint innovation projects, but creates no enforceable obligations. It takes effect on signature and is intended to support future collaboration rather than impose new requirements.

title: EM on EU regulation 389/2012 (13979/22, COM(2022)539)
summary: HM Treasury explains an EU proposal to amend Regulation 389/2012 on excise-duty information exchange and notes it would extend data sharing to duty-paid movements. It says the change would not create new business obligations and is relevant to Northern Ireland under the Protocol. The proposal was expected to take effect from 13 February 2023, but this EM itself imposes no requirements.

title: Publication of Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5, 6, and 7 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published nine web general licenses and their later iterations under the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations for transactions related to the Panamanian seizure of Balboa Bank & Trust. The licenses were already available on OFAC’s website and are now expired, but they also include a reporting requirement for U.S. persons within 10 business days while they were in effect.

title: Publication of Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations Web General License 1A and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published three General Licenses under the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations for the wind-down and liquidation of Banco Continental, S.A. The licenses are now expired, but they showed a time-limited authorization, restrictions on unblocking and other dealings, and a reporting requirement for U.S. persons within 10 business days after wind-down activities end.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 53
summary: OFAC published General License 53 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes U.S. persons to carry out certain transactions needed for Russian diplomatic and consular missions, including employee compensation, subject to stated carve-outs. The license was issued on 2022-11-10 and published on 2022-12-01.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 28A
summary: OFAC published General License 28A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain transactions involving Transkapitalbank and Afghanistan and related correspondent account activity for U.S. financial institutions until 2023-01-18. It also supersedes General License 28. Firms dealing with sanctions-sensitive payments or correspondent banking should update screening and payment processing controls.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – December 2022
summary: Treasury Minutes progress report updating Parliament on the Government’s implementation of accepted Committee of Public Accounts recommendations across many prior sessions. It is an informational progress update, not a rule, supervision notice, or enforcement action. No direct obligations or deadlines are created for firms.

title: Ring-fencing reforms
summary: HM Treasury publishes its response to the independent review of ring-fencing and proprietary trading. It says the government intends to consult in mid-2023 on near-term reforms and to issue a call for evidence in Q1 2023 on aligning the ring-fencing and resolution regimes. This is an awareness paper, not a rule or consultation itself.

title: Treasury Minutes – December 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to the Public Accounts Committee across several topics, including waste crime, regulation after EU exit, whole-of-government accounts, electronic monitoring services, and local air quality breaches. It records government positions and implementation updates, but it does not itself create new regulatory requirements. No direct bank-specific obligation or deadline is set out.

title: Memorandum of Understanding between the UK and the Republic of Chile
summary: HM Treasury published a UK-Chile memorandum of understanding on financial services collaboration. It is a policy paper describing cooperation to share best practices and developments in financial sector policy, regulation and pro-competitive practices, with no new binding obligations or deadlines.

title: Intent To Make Preemption Determination Under the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z)
summary: The CFPB published a request for comment and notice of intent to make a preemption determination under TILA/Regulation Z for a New York State commercial financing law, and may consider similar laws in California, Utah and Virginia. Comments are due by 2023-01-20. It is not yet a binding rule, but may affect state-law disclosure requirements for covered credit transactions.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 54
summary: OFAC published General License 54 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain transactions involving VEON Ltd. debt or equity securities issued before 2022-06-06, and related clearing and settlement activities. Firms must still ensure no other RuHSR restrictions apply, including dealings with blocked persons. The licence was issued on 2022-11-18 and published on 2022-12-16.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determination and Web General Licenses 55, 56, and 57
summary: OFAC published a sanctions determination and three general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The determination expands prohibited services for maritime transport of Russian-origin crude oil, with a price-cap carve-out and a transition period. GLs 55-57 authorize certain otherwise prohibited transactions, including Sakhalin-2-related services, for stated periods.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General License 21
summary: OFAC published Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations General License 21, which authorizes limited safety, environmental, docking, crew safety and emergency repair transactions for specified blocked vessels and persons until 2022-12-15. Firms dealing with the named vessels or counterparties must ensure any permitted payments go to blocked accounts and avoid new commercial contracts, cargo offloading, or other prohibited dealings.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13C
summary: OFAC published General License 13C under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes certain tax, fee, import duty, permit, license, registration and certification payments for U.S. persons and entities they own or control, for ordinary day-to-day operations in Russia, through 2023-03-07. It supersedes General License 13B.

title: Financial Inclusion Report 2021/22
summary: This is HM Treasury’s Financial Inclusion Report 2021/22, an informational policy paper summarising government progress and priorities on access to cash, banking, credit, insurance, fintech, vulnerability, savings and debt support. It does not itself create new obligations. It references the Financial Services and Markets Bill and related policy measures, but is not a rule or consultation.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update
summary: HM Treasury publishes a progress update on its Women in Finance Charter commitments, including its senior female representation as of March 2022 and future internal priorities. It is an informational policy paper for the Treasury’s own signatory commitments, with no new requirements for regulated firms.

title: Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determination
summary: OFAC published a sanctions determination setting a $60 per barrel price cap on crude oil of Russian Federation origin under Executive Order 14071. It took effect on 2022-12-05 and applies to parties involved in the relevant Russia-related oil trade and services restrictions.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8D and 40C
summary: OFAC published two Russia sanctions general licenses, GL 8D and GL 40C, under 31 CFR part 587. GL 8D authorizes certain energy-related transactions involving specified Russian banks and the Central Bank of Russia through 2023-05-15; GL 40C authorizes certain civil-aviation-safety transactions for specified blocked entities. Firms dealing with Russia-linked activity should check the scope and exclusions immediately.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: January 2023
summary: HMT publishes economic evidence for the 2023-24 Pay Review Bodies pay round. It sets out inflation, GDP, labour market and fiscal context to inform public-sector pay recommendations; it does not create regulatory obligations for firms. No action date is specified beyond the January 2023 publication date.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 1, 2, 4, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published Venezuela sanctions general licenses 1, 2, 2A, 4, 4A, 4B and 4C, which authorize certain otherwise prohibited transactions and, for some licenses, require post-transaction reporting. U.S. persons relying on GL 1 must file a detailed report within 10 business days. The publication is relevant to persons dealing with Venezuela-related transactions and sanctioned entities such as CITGO and PDV Holding.

title: UK - US financial services co-operation – statement on the seventh meeting of the Financial Regulatory Working Group
summary: HM Treasury and the U.S. Treasury published a joint statement on the seventh UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting. It summarises discussion topics and cooperation themes only; it does not create new obligations or deadlines.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving Bitzlato
summary: FinCEN issued an order effective 2023-02-01 prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving Bitzlato, a non-US virtual asset service provider found to be of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance. Covered financial institutions and domestic financial institutions must stop the specified transactions from that date.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volumes I and II and related rule changes, effective 2023-01-24. Filers using EDGAR must follow the revised access and filing requirements, including who may sign Form ID and how title/position must be stated. The updated manual is incorporated by reference into the CFR.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 5F and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published updated Venezuela general licenses 5F through 5J authorizing certain transactions, financing, and other dealings in Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% Bond on the stated dates. The latest iteration supersedes the prior one and remains subject to all other Venezuela sanctions restrictions.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 14, 15, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published on its website Venezuela general licenses 14, 15, 15A, 15B and 15C, which authorize specified transactions otherwise prohibited under Venezuela sanctions. The licenses affect certain US government business and certain payment/card/remittance activities involving named Venezuelan banks, and are relevant immediately to sanctions screening and transaction handling.

title: Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (Regulation X); Digital Mortgage Comparison-Shopping Platforms and Related Payments to Operators
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion explaining how RESPA section 8 applies to digital mortgage comparison-shopping platforms. Operators may violate the anti-kickback/referral fee rules if they steer consumers using non-neutral ranking or placement in return for payments. It is effective immediately on 2023-02-13 and affects platform operators and mortgage-related settlement service providers.

title: Determination Regarding Excepted Foreign States
summary: Treasury determined that the United Kingdom and New Zealand are ‘excepted foreign states’ for CFIUS purposes, effective 2023-02-10. This affects foreign investment screening status under the U.S. investment security regime and remains in place unless CFIUS acts again.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 31B
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 31B, which authorizes certain U.S. persons to transact with specified Venezuelan National Assembly-related persons and entities, and replaces General License 31A. It is effective from 2023-01-09. Firms dealing with Venezuela-related counterparties should check sanctions screening and transaction permissions immediately.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 16, 17, 18, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC republishes seven Venezuela general licenses covering certain transactions with specified Venezuelan banks and personal remittances, including successive replacements of earlier licenses. The licenses authorize activity through stated expiry dates and set conditions and exclusions for U.S. financial institutions and others dealing with blocked persons. Firms must check whether any Venezuela-related activity is covered before relying on these licenses.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 21A and 21B
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 21A and 21B under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, authorizing limited safety, crew welfare, emergency repair, and environmental mitigation transactions for specified blocked vessels and related persons. GL 21A was effective until 2023-01-14 and was superseded by GL 21B, which runs until 2023-04-13. Firms dealing with the named vessels or persons must follow the license limits.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 6C, 28B, and 54A
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 6C, 28B and 54A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize specified Russia-related transactions, including certain agricultural, medical and COVID-19-related dealings, and wind-down/rejection activity involving TKB entities and Afghanistan, with effective dates from 2023-01-17. Firms dealing with Russia, sanctioned parties or cross-border payments should update sanctions screening and procedures.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, and 28
summary: OFAC published six Venezuela general licenses that authorize specified transactions and exports involving the Government of Venezuela, including telecoms, mail, internet communications, diplomatic/consular funds transfers, and certain oilfield-related activities. These licenses were previously issued on OFAC’s website and are effective as stated in the individual licenses; one listed license had already expired.

title: Annual Information Return/Reports
summary: The US Departments of Labor and Treasury, plus PBGC, issued final revisions to Form 5500 and Form 5500-SF annual return/report forms and instructions for employee benefit plans. The changes apply to plan years beginning on or after 2023-01-01 and affect reporting by pension and welfare benefit plans, plan sponsors, administrators and service providers subject to ERISA and the Code.

title: Basic bank accounts: July 2021 to June 2022
summary: HM Treasury published annual statistics on basic bank accounts for July 2021 to June 2022. It reports account openings, closures, upgrades and refusals at the nine UK designated providers under the Payment Account Regulations, and notes FCA supervision of compliance. It does not itself change rules or deadlines.

title: Order Designating the Unique Product Identifier and Product Classification System To Be Used in Recordkeeping and Swap Data Reporting
summary: The CFTC designated Derivatives Service Bureau unique product identifiers and product classification system for swaps in the credit, equity, foreign exchange and interest rate asset classes. Registered entities and swap counterparties must use these identifiers for certain swap recordkeeping and data reporting requirements. The order is effective February 24, 2023.

title: Spring Budget 2023 customs measures
summary: HMRC/HMT published a policy paper setting out Spring Budget 2023 customs measures to simplify import and export processes. It explains the package and proposes further customs reform ideas, informed by a prior call for evidence. It does not itself create binding requirements or set a compliance date.

title: Spring Budget 2023 – Disability White Paper Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet summarising disability reforms announced in the Health and Disability White Paper. It is a policy/communications document only and does not create regulatory obligations for firms. No action date or compliance deadline is stated.

title: Government response to the 2022 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response to the OBR’s Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report discusses the UK government’s fiscal strategy, debt and borrowing outlook, and measures to manage public finances. It is informational only and does not create binding requirements for firms. No compliance date or direct obligation is set for banks or other regulated firms.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Digital Technologies
summary: HM Government’s review sets out recommendations for a more pro-innovation UK approach to digital technologies, including AI, data access, autonomous vehicles, drones, cyber security, and space/satellite. It is a policy report, not a binding rule, and points to possible future legislation and further policy work rather than immediate obligations.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8F, 13D, 60, and 61
summary: OFAC published web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited Russia-related transactions for limited periods and purposes. GL 8F covers certain energy-related transactions through 2023-05-16; GL 13D permits some routine administrative transactions through 2023-06-06; GLs 60 and 61 were also published. Sanctions teams must check scope, expiry and any superseded licenses.

title: Bulletin 2023-01: Unfair Billing and Collection Practices After Bankruptcy Discharges of Certain Student Loan Debts
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin and policy guidance warning student-loan servicers not to bill or collect on private education loans that were discharged in bankruptcy. It applies immediately from 2023-03-23 and says CFPB examiners will scrutinize servicing practices and expect remedial action, including lookbacks and refunds, where firms wrongly resumed collection after discharge orders.

title: Distilled Spirits Plants
summary: This CFR correction republishes a text fix to 27 CFR Part 19 for distilled spirits plants. The corrected rule states that a proprietor must prepay tax when a withdrawal would push outstanding tax liability above bond coverage limits. It is an editorial/technical correction, effective as part of the CFR update rather than a new policy change.

title: General Rules and Regulations, Securities Act of 1933
summary: This SEC/Office of the Federal Register correction updates two Securities Act rules in 17 CFR Part 230 by fixing editorial text in §§ 230.482 and 230.498. It affects SEC-regulated securities offering disclosures and related prospectus materials. There is no substantive policy change, but firms should note the corrected codified text as of the publication date.

title: Regulation S-T-General Rules and Regulations for Electronic Filings
summary: This CFR correction republished an SEC Regulation S-T definition, reinstating the term “Interactive Data Financial Report” in 17 CFR Part 232. It applies to SEC electronic filing requirements and is effective as a codified text correction rather than a new policy change.

title: Income Taxes
summary: This CFR correction updates Title 26, Part 1 to fix an editorial/technical error in the income tax regulations, specifically the temporary partner distributive share provision in § 1.704-1T. It applies to tax rulebook codification rather than introducing new substantive requirements.

title: Publication of Syria Web General License 23
summary: OFAC published Syria General License 23, authorizing certain earthquake-relief transactions otherwise prohibited by the Syrian Sanctions Regulations through 2023-08-08. U.S. financial institutions and U.S.-registered money transmitters may rely on originators for funds transfers within the license, subject to sanctions-screening limits and other exclusions.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant for 2023-24
summary: This is a statutory report to Parliament under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 setting out the Royal Trustees’ determination of the Sovereign Grant for 2023-24 and how it was calculated. It does not impose obligations on regulated firms. It is relevant only as a public-law/UK government finance publication, with no direct compliance deadline for banks.

title: HM Treasury Evaluation Strategy
summary: HM Treasury sets out its overall strategy for using evaluation in policy-making and for supporting evaluation across government. It is an internal policy paper with no firm-facing rules, obligations, or deadlines.

title: General Rules and Regulations, Securities Exchange Act of 1934
summary: The SEC published a CFR correction to 17 CFR Part 240, reinstating omitted text in Rule 13e-100 for Schedule 13E-3 filing/signature instructions under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. This is an editorial technical fix, not a substantive policy change, but it affects firms using this filing form from publication onward.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 29, 30, 30A, 31, and 31A
summary: OFAC published five Venezuela general licenses in the Federal Register, reflecting authorizations for certain transactions involving the Government of Venezuela, mainly for NGOs and humanitarian, democracy, education, development, and environmental activities. The licenses are already available on OFAC’s website and are part of the Venezuela sanctions regime; firms dealing with Venezuela should assess whether their activity falls within the authorizations and conditions.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted amendments updating the EDGAR Filer Manual and related filing rules, effective 2023-04-20. The changes affect filers submitting electronically to EDGAR, including new XBRL taxonomies, updated tagging for compensation and trading disclosures, revised Form 144 filing hours, and a new checkbox for Form 13F-CTR/A.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 62, 63, 64, and 65
summary: OFAC published four general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. They authorize limited wind-down, divestment, transfer, and related transaction activity involving specified Russian persons and related debt, equity, and derivatives, with some permissions expiring on 2023-07-11. Sanctions teams, payments, and operations should confirm whether any activity is covered and any blocked-account handling is required.

title: Interagency Policy Statement on Allowances for Credit Losses (Revised April 2023)
summary: The OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC and NCUA revised their interagency policy statement on allowances for credit losses to remove references to troubled debt restructurings and align it with updated U.S. GAAP. It applies to supervised depository institutions and credit unions using CECL. The statement was issued on 2023-04-27 and is effective immediately as published.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2021-22
summary: HM Treasury publishes examples of best practice for government annual reports and accounts for 2021-22, focusing on performance, accountability and financial information. It is guidance-only and aimed at entities preparing ARAs across government, with no new legal or reporting requirements. The paper points to the Government Financial Reporting Review and the 2022-23 FReM as context.

title: Joint Statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 10 May 2023
summary: This is a joint statement from the UK and European Commission noting progress on Financial Provisions work streams related to invoices sent by the EU to the UK under the Financial Settlement. It is informational only and does not create or change any firm obligations.

title: Spring Finance Bill 2023: Public Bill Committee
summary: A Finance Bill amendment would expand the exceptions to the trustee income tax de minimis rules in ITA 2007 by excluding certain pension funds from the reduction calculation. It affects trusts holding registered pension schemes, superannuation funds and certain occupational pension schemes. No action date is stated in the text.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2023
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports on education, NHS backlogs, excess votes, COVID support schemes and DVLA backlogs. It records government responses and target implementation dates such as December 2023 for final evaluations of CJRS and SEISS, but does not itself change rules for firms.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General License O
summary: OFAC published General License O under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations and Executive Order 13846. It authorizes certain wind-down, docking, crew-safety, emergency repair and environmental mitigation transactions for specified blocked vessels and related entities through 2023-06-30, with blocked payments to be made into blocked accounts and reported to OFAC. New contracts and offloading Iranian-origin petroleum remain prohibited.

title: Technical Amendments to Form BD and Form BDW
summary: The SEC made technical amendments to Form BD and Form BDW, updating the list of SROs and jurisdictions, including Guam, and conforming the definition of “jurisdiction.” The changes are effective immediately on 2023-05-23 and affect broker-dealer registration and withdrawal filings.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Life Sciences and the government response
summary: This is a UK government review and response on how regulation should better support life sciences innovation, including medicines, devices, AI/digital tools, engineering biology and novel foods. It recommends future policy and regulator improvements, but does not itself create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Financial Services & Markets Bill – Overseas Central Counterparties
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper explaining two technical amendments to the Financial Services and Markets Bill on overseas central counterparties. The changes would help UK firms continue using certain non-UK CCPs after the CCP run-off regime exit date of 1 July 2023, if Parliament approves them.

title: Publication of Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 1 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published web text for four general licenses under its cyber-related, non-proliferation and hostages/wrongfully detained sanctions programs. The licenses authorize limited transactions with the FSB and related activities, while preserving key prohibitions. Sanctions teams and operations should use the current license text for screening and permitted-dealing decisions; this is effective as published and reflects prior issuances.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 13E, 66, 67, and 68
summary: OFAC published four web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize limited transactions, including certain administrative payments, wind-down activity, and divestment or settlement transactions involving Public Joint Stock Company Polyus, with expiry dates in August 2023 and July 2023 for one license. U.S. persons and entities they own or control should check scope and expiry before acting.

title: Publication of Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General License 2 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC republished Belarus sanctions general licenses 2 and 2A through 2H. The licenses authorize certain transactions involving named Belarusian entities and require U.S. persons to file a report within 15 days after transactions over $10,000 under the license. Firms dealing with Belarus-linked persons or property should confirm whether any activity is covered and whether reporting is due.

title: Review of the Oil and Gas Fiscal Regime: Terms of Reference
summary: HM Treasury published terms of reference for a review of the UK oil and gas fiscal regime. It is a policy paper setting out the review’s context, objectives and scope, not a rule or consultation with obligations. It is relevant mainly for awareness to firms exposed to the oil and gas sector.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 8L
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 8L, replacing GL 8K and authorizing certain PdVSA-related transactions for specified covered entities until 2023-11-19. The license is limited to essential operations/safe wind-down activities and excludes drilling, petroleum trade, insurance for those activities, new personnel, dividends, loans, and other blocked-person dealings.

title: Data Reporting Services Regulations 2023 - Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury published a near-final draft Statutory Instrument and policy note to replace retained EU law for Data Reporting Service Providers, supporting a UK consolidated tape and updating the rules for APAs, ARMs and CTPs. It invites technical comments by 21 August 2023. The measure is part of the Smarter Regulatory Framework and will affect firms that use or provide data reporting services.

title: Summary of Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting February 2023
summary: This is a government policy paper summarising the tenth meeting of the Financial Inclusion Policy Forum. It is informational only and does not create or change requirements for firms. No action or deadline is stated.

title: Investment Research Review
summary: HM Treasury published the Investment Research Review, an independent policy paper by Rachel Kent on the UK investment research market and capital markets competitiveness. It sets out recommendations to government, the FCA and industry, including a research platform, wider access for retail investors, issuer-sponsored research code of conduct, and review of IPO-related rules. It is an outcome paper and does not itself create rules.

title: Digitisation Taskforce
summary: HMT’s Digitisation Taskforce policy paper sets out an interim report and invites industry feedback on proposals to modernise the UK shareholding framework, including eliminating paper share certificates and expanding digitisation options. It is an open-engagement policy paper rather than a binding rule. Feedback on the interim report was requested by 25 September 2023, with final recommendations due in spring 2024.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updates to EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and related rules, effective 2023-07-18. The changes support EDGAR Release 23.2, new Form SD exhibit types for resource extraction disclosures, updated XBRL taxonomies, and stricter taxonomy-version requirements for electronic filings. Filers using EDGAR should update filing processes immediately.

title: Publication of Covid-Related Web General Licenses Related to Syria Sanctions Regulations, Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, and Venezuela Sanctions Regulations.
summary: OFAC published three general licenses extending until 2024 certain COVID-19-related transactions under the Syria, Iran/Global Terrorism, and Venezuela sanctions regulations. The licenses authorize specified exports, imports, and dealings for COVID-19 prevention, diagnosis, or treatment, and replace earlier versions effective June 14, 2023. Firms dealing with sanctioned jurisdictions or persons should review current authorizations immediately.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General License P
summary: OFAC published General License P under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, authorizing wind-down transactions involving Navyan Abr Arvan Private Limited Company or Arvancloud Global Technologies L.L.C. The licence applied through 2023-07-06 and does not authorize other Iran sanctions-prohibited transactions. Firms with Iran-related activities or payments into blocked accounts should confirm sanctions handling and expiry effects.

title: Additional Guidance on Low-Income Communities Bonus Credit Program
summary: The IRS/Treasury published a correction to the final rule on the Low-Income Communities Bonus Credit Program, fixing amendatory instruction 2 in 26 CFR Part 1. This affects the codified text already issued in the earlier final rule and is relevant to entities relying on the program's tax-credit guidance.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13F
summary: OFAC published General License 13F under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes certain tax, fee, import duty, and licensing payments by U.S. persons and entities owned or controlled by U.S. persons for day-to-day operations in Russia, until 2023-11-08. GL 13E was superseded. Sanctions teams must check scope immediately.

title: Publication of Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8 and 9
summary: OFAC published Belarus Sanctions Regulations general licenses 8 and 9. They authorize certain wind-down transactions with designated Belarusian entities and, for Belavia, certain civil aviation safety-related transactions, each only until the stated expiry dates. Firms dealing with sanctioned persons must check the scope, blocked-account requirements and any separate export controls.

title: Treasury Minutes - September 2023
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports across several government departments, including justice, health, transport, home affairs and HMRC. It records government responses and target implementation dates for recommendations, but does not itself create regulatory obligations for firms. Relevant dates mentioned include March 2024 and January 2024 for government actions.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 42
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 42, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions needed to negotiate settlement agreements with specified Venezuelan National Assembly-related persons and certain Venezuela debt matters. It does not authorize dealings with the Maduro National Constituent Assembly or the 2021 National Assembly. Effective from the license issue date of 2023-05-01.

title: The Commission's Privacy Act Regulations
summary: The SEC adopted updated Privacy Act regulations for SEC records and Privacy Act requests. The final rule clarifies procedures, allows electronic identity verification, adjusts response times and fee provisions, and removes obsolete text. It is effective 2023-10-26.

title: EM on a UK/EU TCA Specialised Committee decision (COM(2023)527)
summary: HM Treasury published an explanatory memorandum on an EU Council decision for the UK/EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement Specialised Committee to adopt changes enabling UK association to Horizon Europe and Copernicus from 1 January 2024. It explains eligibility, funding treatment for 2021-2023 calls, and a clawback mechanism, but it is not itself a rule or obligation for firms.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 55A and 72
summary: OFAC published two Russian sanctions general licenses: GL 55A authorizes certain Sakhalin-2-related maritime transport transactions for importation into Japan until 2024-06-28, and GL 72 authorizes wind-down transactions involving specified newly blocked entities until 2023-12-13. Both are subject to stated exclusions and sanctions restrictions.

title: Payment service contract termination rule changes: implementation, timings, and next steps
summary: HM Treasury sets out how it will amend the Payment Services Regulations 2017 to extend payment account/framework contract termination notice to 90 days and require clear, tailored reasons for termination, subject to limited exceptions. The policy statement clarifies scope, expected practice, and next legislative steps for payment service providers, including banks and other firms with payment accounts.

title: Consumer Information Requests to Large Banks and Credit Unions
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion on section 1034(c) of the Consumer Financial Protection Act, explaining that large banks and credit unions must timely respond to consumer requests for account information, subject to limited exceptions. It is effective immediately as of 2023-10-16, and the CFPB said it does not intend to seek monetary relief for pre-2024 violations.

title: Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Bill 2022: overarching documents
summary: This is an HMT policy paper page collecting background documents for the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Bill/Act, including the draft bill and fact sheets on the register of overseas entities, unexplained wealth orders and sanctions. It is informational only and does not itself create obligations.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 73
summary: OFAC published General License 73 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes limited safety, crew-welfare, emergency repair, and environmental mitigation transactions involving two blocked vessels through 2024-01-08, subject to restrictions and blocked-account payment rules. Firms dealing with the listed persons, vessels, or related transactions must check sanctions permissions before acting.

title: Extending the transitional period for third country benchmarks in the UK
summary: HM Treasury has laid a statutory instrument extending the UK Benchmarks Regulation transitional period for third-country benchmarks from 31 December 2025 to 31 December 2030. The change comes into force on 1 January 2024 and affects firms using or relying on third-country benchmarks in the UK.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 3I, 5M, 9H, 43, 44, and 45
summary: OFAC published web versions of six Venezuela general licenses under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize certain otherwise prohibited transactions in specified bonds and related activities, with some superseding earlier licenses and one license expiring on 2024-04-18. Firms dealing in Venezuela-related persons or securities should confirm transaction permissibility against the updated licenses.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Advanced Manufacturing
summary: This is a UK government review report on how regulation and standards could better support advanced manufacturing innovation, including automation, hydrogen, clean fuels, recycling and building materials. It makes policy recommendations for government and regulators; it does not itself change rules or impose deadlines.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 13G, 74, 75, and 76.
summary: OFAC published four Russian sanctions general licenses covering certain administrative transactions, wind-down/rejection activity involving East-West United Bank, and related divestment/transfer permissions. The licenses were issued on 2023-11-02 and generally expire on 2024-01-31. U.S. persons and covered entities should check whether their Russia-related transactions now fall within these temporary authorizations.

title: UK Retail Disclosure Framework – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury publishes a near-final draft statutory instrument and policy note for a new UK retail disclosure framework for Consumer Composite Investments under the Designated Activities Regime. It is replacing retained EU PRIIPs rules and gives the FCA rule-making powers and related supervision/enforcement provisions. Technical comments on the draft are invited by 2024-01-10.

title: Autumn Statement 2023: National Insurance Factsheet
summary: UK government factsheet announcing National Insurance cuts for employees and the self-employed, and the abolition of Class 2 NICs as part of the Autumn Statement 2023. It is informational only and does not itself create the tax change or set an implementation deadline.

title: The mortgage guarantee scheme
summary: HM Treasury’s policy paper announces and explains a mortgage guarantee scheme to support homeownership and high loan-to-value lending. It is descriptive and consultative in tone, setting out the intended design and policy rationale, but it does not itself impose binding requirements or deadlines on lenders.

title: Further detail on HMT analysis of borrowing and interest rates
summary: HMT published a policy paper with a methodological annex and supplementary data explaining how it estimates the impact of additional government borrowing on interest rates. It is informational only and does not create obligations for firms.

title: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (The Ombudsman Scheme) Regulations 2024 – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury publishes a draft statutory instrument and policy note to extend the Financial Ombudsman Service’s fee-charging scope so it can charge claims management companies and other professional representatives, not just respondent firms. It is tied to the FOS Plans and Budget consultation closing on 2024-01-30, and HM Treasury says it intends to legislate before the FOS makes new charging rules.

title: Decision No 1/2023 of the Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement adopting Protocols I and II and amending Annex 47 to the Trade and Cooperation Agreement
summary: This EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement decision adopts Protocols I and II and amends Annex 47. It confirms UK participation and contribution terms for certain Union programmes from 1 January 2024, including Horizon Europe-related funding mechanics. Relevant teams should note the updated participation, contribution, and call-for-funds rules for affected UK entities and programme activities.

title: EM about an amendment to EU decision 2021/512 (COM(2023)704)
summary: HM Treasury explains an EU proposal to extend the UK’s Northern Ireland VAT fuel derogation until 31 December 2026. It would keep the flat-rate method allowing businesses to reclaim VAT on fuel for company cars without full mileage records. This is an explanatory memorandum only, not the binding decision itself.

title: Response to the VRP Working Group’s Blueprint for non-sweeping VRPs
summary: HMT/PSR/FCA publish the JROC response to the industry blueprint for phased rollout of non-sweeping VRPs in open banking. It discusses future use cases, consumer protection and commercial model issues, but does not itself create binding requirements or dates for firms.

title: Joint Regulatory Oversight Committee update on actions to enable the next phase of open banking in the UK
summary: The JROC provides a progress update on work to move UK open banking into its next phase, including plans for a future entity, governance, funding and phased development of new services. It is an update and roadmap rather than a binding rule, with further decisions and proposals expected in 2024.

title: Technical note: Electricity Generator Levy – new investment exemption
summary: HM Treasury published a technical note on a new investment exemption for the UK Electricity Generator Levy. Where the substantive decision to proceed with a new generating station or expansion is made on or after 22 November 2023, the new capacity or station receipts may be exempt from EGL. It is an interpretive note, not formal guidance; HMRC will issue that separately.

title: Publication of Syria-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 1, 2, and 3
summary: OFAC published Syria-related general licenses 1, 2 and 3 under 31 CFR part 569. The licenses authorize specified transactions for U.S. government official business, certain wind-down activities involving Turkish ministries, and official activities of certain international organizations, subject to stated limits. This is a sanctions update affecting firms dealing in Syria-/Turkey-related transactions and should be applied immediately.

title: Notification of Inflation Adjustments for Civil Money Penalties
summary: The OCC updates 2024 maximum civil money penalties for inflation under federal penalty inflation statutes. The new amounts apply to OCC penalties assessed on or after 2024-01-08 for conduct on or after 2015-11-02, including national banks and Federal savings associations.

title: Policy Design Document
summary: HM Treasury’s policy design document sets out the proposed design, mandate, capitalisation and operating model for the UK Infrastructure Bank, including its headquarters, funding capacity and intended areas of focus. It is an informational policy paper about a future institution, not a binding rule. The document notes that legislation will be brought forward later to place the Bank on a statutory footing.

title: Central Counterparties Special Resolution Regime Code of Practice
summary: The UK Treasury has issued a Code of Practice under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 for the CCP special resolution regime. It explains how the Bank of England and Treasury may use CCP resolution powers, including bridge CCPs, and the objectives and governance they must consider. It applies to UK CCP resolution and reflects international resolution standards.

title: Sovereign Infrastructure Guarantee
summary: HM Treasury and UK Infrastructure Bank have executed an amendment and restatement of the Sovereign Infrastructure Guarantee. This is a binding contractual/public guarantee document affecting the UK state-backed infrastructure financing arrangement, effective from the agreement date. No filing or compliance deadline is stated, but the document is legally operative for the parties.
